They are now gated behind `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` and return `404` in production so they cannot be exploited even if the deployment exposes them.\n    -   `/api/openai/v1/audio/transcriptions` now requires authentication (signed session cookie or `Authorization: Bearer ptbk_…` API key), enforces a 25 MB upload size limit, validates the `model` parameter against an allowlist of supported OpenAI transcription models (`gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, `whisper-1`), validates `language` against ISO-639-1, and truncates the optional transcription `prompt` to 800 characters.\n    -   `/api/elevenlabs/tts` now requires authentication and validates the caller-supplied `voiceId` against the strict ElevenLabs format (15–40 alphanumeric characters), preventing path-segment injection into the upstream URL and rejecting unknown voices that would still bill the ElevenLabs account.\n    -   `/api/images/[filename]` now requires authentication and validates `modelName`, `size`, `quality`, and `style` query parameters against fixed allowlists (DALL·E / Gemini image models, supported sizes, `standard`/`hd`, `vivid`/`natural`) before forwarding to the paid image generation provider.\n    -   The shared guard applies a per-identity sliding-window rate limit on top of authentication — by username for cookie sessions, by hashed API key for bearer auth, and by request IP for any anonymous fallback. Budgets are tier-specific (60/min for transcription and TTS, 20/min for image generation), so a single compromised account cannot sustain large bills. Rejected requests receive `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header.\n\n-   Fixed authentication bypass in Agents Server `validateApiKey`: the helper previously treated the presence of any `sessionToken` cookie as proof of a valid browser session, so any client could forge `Cookie: sessionToken=anything` and gain unauthenticated access to every endpoint behind `validateApiKey` (including the OpenAI-compatible chat-completion routes that consume server-side API credits). The helper now parses the cookie value with the existing `parseSessionToken` HMAC-signature verifier and only accepts the request when the signature matches, restoring the original intent of the browser-session shortcut without trusting attacker-supplied cookies.\n\n-   Optimized Agents Server directory and chat-sidebar reads for standalone VPS and Supabase deployments:\n\n    -   Added SQLite read indexes for active agent/folder directory scans, chat sidebar lists, and active chat job/timeout polling used by the homepage, agent navigation, and chat pages.\n    -   Added matching PostgreSQL indexes for active agent/folder directory reads and creation-time chat sidebar ordering.\n    -   Invalidated cached active organization snapshots after agent source, visibility, create, delete, and restore mutations so optimized homepage/menu data refreshes immediately.\n\n-   Fixed timing attack vulnerability in Agents Server admin password verification: all three comparison sites (`isUserGlobalAdmin`, `getCurrentUser`, `authenticateUser`) now use a shared `isAdminPasswordEqual` utility that calls Node.js's `timingSafeEqual` (from the `crypto` module) instead of JavaScript's `===` operator, preventing character-by-character password inference via response-time measurement.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server durable chat progress so new agent responses show structured real progress from the queued and preparation phases instead of a synthetic immediate pre-answer:\n\n    -   Queued assistant placeholders now render a progress card with current step, next step, and checklist state.\n    -   The durable chat worker updates that card while it reads context, prepares the agent, checks available tools/inputs, and starts the response.\n    -   The `agent_progress` tool instructions now ask the real agent to report concise user-facing decisions, actions, and results without exposing hidden chain-of-thought or raw technical details.\n\n-   Fixed SSRF vulnerability in the Agents Server `/api/scrape` endpoint:\n\n    -   The endpoint now requires authentication — unauthenticated requests receive a `401 Unauthorized` response.\n    -   Added URL validation via a new `assertSafeUrl` utility that rejects non-HTTP(S) schemes and destination hostnames that resolve to private/internal IP ranges (RFC 1918: `10.x`, `172.16–31.x`, `192.168.x`; loopback `127.x`; link-local / cloud-metadata `169.254.x`; shared address space `100.64.x`; IPv6 ULA, link-local, and loopback). Blocked requests receive a `400 Bad Request` response.\n\n-   Fixed package publishing for `@promptbook/cli` by marking the `ptbk coder server` HTTP/UI helpers as CLI-only instead of never-publishable, matching the existing CLI command import chain.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder find-unwritten` command that lists all prompt sections whose body still contains the `@@@` authoring placeholder:\n\n    -   Prints a summary line (done / for agent / to be written counts) followed by a numbered list of unwritten prompts with their file path, line number, and first summary line.\n    -   Accepts `--priority <n>` to apply the same minimum-priority filter used by `ptbk coder run`.\n    -   Reuses the existing `listPromptsToBeWritten` / `printPromptsToBeWritten` utilities so the detection logic stays in one place.\n\n-   Added `--agent <agent-book-path>` option to `ptbk coder run` and `ptbk coder server`:\n\n    -   Accepts a path to a `.book` file (relative to the current working directory) whose compiled system message is prepended to each coding prompt before the task text.\n    -   Can be combined with `--context`: the agent system message is inserted first, followed by the task prompt, and finally the context — so the harness sees agent instructions → task → additional context.\n    -   Example: `ptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh --context AGENTS.md --agent agents/coding-expert.book`\n\n-   `ptbk coder init` now automatically generates 5 prompt boilerplate files after setting up the project configuration.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder server` command that runs the same prompt-processing logic as `ptbk coder run` but keeps the process alive and serves a kanban web UI on a configurable port (default `4441`):\n\n    -   The server polls for new prompt files every 5 seconds instead of exiting when all prompts are done or none are ready, making it suitable as a long-running background service.\n    -   A kanban board at `http://localhost:4441` shows all prompt sections grouped into four columns: **To Do**, **Not Ready**, **Done**, and **Failed**.\n    -   Each card is clickable and opens a Trello-style edit modal where the prompt text can be modified and saved back to the source file immediately.\n    -   A **Play / Pause** button in the browser header is kept in sync with the CLI pause state; clicking it calls the same `requestPause` / `requestResume` functions used by the `p` key in the terminal.\n    -   The HTTP server exposes a small REST API: `GET /api/prompts`, `GET /api/status`, `POST /api/pause`, `POST /api/resume`, and `PUT /api/prompts/update`.\n    -   All options from `ptbk coder run` are supported (`--harness`, `--model`, `--thinking-level`, `--context`, `--test`, `--wait`, `--priority`, `--no-commit`, etc.) plus a new `--port` option (or `PTBK_CODER_SERVER_PORT` env var).\n    -   The frontend source lives in `apps/coder-server/index.html` and is served inline by the Node.js HTTP server (no build step required).\n\n-   Added a VSCode extension (`apps/vscode-extension`) for the Book language that provides syntax highlighting for `.book` and `.ptbk` files. The TextMate grammar (`syntaxes/book.tmLanguage.json`) is dynamically generated from `COMMITMENT_REGISTRY` by running `npm run generate-vscode-grammar`, ensuring the extension always reflects the current set of commitment keywords. Publishing to the Visual Studio Code Marketplace is available through `npm run build:vscode-extension -- --publish`, which generates the grammar, syncs a Marketplace-safe extension version from the root `package.json`, publishes with `vsce`, and creates the VSIX artifact.\n\n-   Fixed `<BookEditor/>` syntax highlighting incorrectly highlighting the local part of email addresses (e.g. `team@foo.bar`) as agent references. `@`-style references now require whitespace or start-of-line before the `@` sign, so only `@Paul` (with preceding whitespace) is highlighted, not `team@foo.bar`. Removed a now-redundant manual preceding-character check that duplicated this logic.\n\n-   Improved `<BookEditor/>` syntax highlighting to dynamically detect commitments — any line starting with one or more all-uppercase words (minimum 2 characters each) is now highlighted as a commitment keyword, without relying on a hardcoded list of known commitment types. Lines starting with a dash or a single uppercase letter are not affected. Special commitment types (`NOTE`, `NOTES`, `NONCE`, `TODO`) retain their distinct colors, and `FROM`/`IMPORT`/`IMPORTS`/`TEAM` retain agent-reference link highlighting.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server VPS installation failing on the first run with a Node.js out-of-memory crash during the Next.js production build. The `ptbk agents-server build` command now passes `--max-old-space-size=4096` in `NODE_OPTIONS` when spawning the webpack compilation process, allowing the ~1.9 GiB peak heap usage to succeed within the swap-backed memory budget enforced by the installer. Existing `NODE_OPTIONS` values are preserved; the flag is only injected when no `--max-old-space-size` is already set.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server file upload URLs for self-contained S3 to hide the internal bucket name, path prefix, and directory structure. Files are now stored under a content-addressed key (`{hash[0]}/{hash[1]}/{sha256}/{filename}`) and served through a new Next.js proxy route (`/s3/{hex}/{hex}/{hash}/{filename}`) so the public URL is unguessable and reveals no internal storage details. Old-style URLs (e.g. `/s3/promptbook-files/ptbk-agents/user/files/…`) remain accessible for backwards compatibility.\n\n-   Fixed citation source previews in Agents Server chat failing silently when the target page blocks iframe embedding via `X-Frame-Options` (e.g. `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`). The chat modal now checks embeddability server-side before rendering and falls back to a server-taken screenshot with an \"Open in new tab\" link when the page cannot be framed.\n\n-   Optimized Agents Server database layer to prevent the server from becoming unresponsive under load:\n\n    -   Added `connectionTimeoutMillis` (15 s) to the shared PostgreSQL connection pool so queries fail fast when all connections are busy instead of queuing indefinitely — the root cause of the server becoming completely unresponsive after a period of high traffic.\n    -   Increased the default pool size from 10 to 20 connections (configurable via `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` environment variable) to handle more concurrent chat-stream polling and atomic-SQL operations without exhausting the pool.\n    -   Added `idleTimeoutMillis` (30 s) and `allowExitOnIdle` so unused connections are closed promptly, keeping memory and socket usage low.\n    -   Added a pool `error` event handler so unexpected errors on idle clients are logged instead of propagating as unhandled exceptions that can corrupt the pool state.\n    -   Added a 30-second hard timeout to every Supabase HTTP request via a custom `fetch` wrapper on the server-side Supabase client. Without this, a slow or temporarily unreachable PostgREST endpoint would cause Supabase queries to hang indefinitely, holding Node.js event-loop resources and contributing to the gradual unresponsiveness over time.\n\n-   Added `isVerbose` option to `CliAgent` so callers can enable the same harness-level console output that `ptbk agent exec --verbose` produces without spawning the CLI. `LiteAgent` already supported `isVerbose`; both classes now expose the option consistently.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat runner not including the agent's initial message (defined via `INITIAL MESSAGE` commitment) in the queued book file when a user sends their first message. The local and external chat runners now prepend the agent's initial message as the opening `MESSAGE @Agent` block so the agent runner sees the full conversation context from the start.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat messages being silently cropped when the agent response contained a line starting with a single uppercase ASCII letter followed by lowercase text (e.g. \"V části...\" in Czech). `Book.parse` was incorrectly treating such lines as commitment headers due to an overly permissive regex in `parseCommitmentHeader`. The fix tightens the regex to require at least two characters in the first keyword word, which prevents common natural-language words like \"V\" (Czech for \"in\") or \"A\" / \"I\" in English from being mistaken for commitment markers.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server chat tray ordering from last-activity time to creation time so chats stay in their chronological position and browsing an older chat no longer moves it to the top of the list.\n\n-   Optimized animated avatar rendering performance in Agents Server to fix 1–2 fps drops when multiple avatars are visible:\n\n    -   Throttled the shared animation loop to ~24 fps (from the display refresh rate of 60 fps+) via a frame-interval gate in `avatarAnimationScheduler.ts`. Animated octopus visuals change slowly enough that 24 fps is perceptually identical to 60 fps while reducing total render work by ~60%.\n    -   Cached stable per-avatar data (morphology profile, animation phase, tentacle profiles, eye phase offsets) using a `WeakMap` keyed on the `createRandom` factory reference in `octopus3dAvatarVisual`, `octopus3d2AvatarVisual`, and `octopus3d3AvatarVisual`. These values are deterministic given the avatar definition and were previously recomputed on every frame.\n    -   Replaced `context.filter = 'blur()'` shadow effects in all six affected visuals (`octopus3d`, `octopus3d2`, `octopus3d3`, `minecraft`, `minecraft2`, `fractal`) with equivalent gradient-based approximations. CSS filter blur forces the browser into a full software rasterization pass on every frame; the gradient alternative is hardware-accelerated and visually equivalent.\n    -   Added `\"ts-node\": { \"transpileOnly\": true }` to `tsconfig.json` so the CLI integration test (`ts-node src/cli/test/ptbk.ts --help`) skips full type-checking during execution. Type correctness is still enforced by the dedicated `test-types` step; this change brings the CLI startup from an uncapped compile pass (> 5 min on Windows) down to ~20 seconds.\n\n-   Further optimized animated avatar rendering performance in Agents Server, building on the earlier 24 fps throttle and stable-state cache. With twelve animated octopus avatars on a single page the previous pass still left the UI at 1–2 fps because every visible avatar fired on the same animation frame and the per-frame mesh sampling cost remained heavy:\n\n    -   Interleaved listeners in `avatarAnimationScheduler.ts` so animated avatars no longer all render on the same animation frame. Each listener now tracks its own last-run timestamp, new listeners are phase-staggered at registration, and the shared loop runs at most `MAX_AVATAR_LISTENERS_PER_FRAME` (= 2) listeners per `requestAnimationFrame`, scheduling the rest on subsequent frames. Each avatar still reaches the 24 fps target individually; total per-frame work is bounded regardless of how many avatars are visible.\n    -   Added per-frame corner-grid sample caching to `octopus3d3AvatarVisual` and `octopus3d2AvatarVisual`. The mesh patch loop previously called `sampleContinuousOctopusSurfacePoint` / `sampleBlobbyOctopusSurfacePoint` for each of the four corners of every patch (16×40×4 = 2 560 samples per frame for `octopus3d3`), even though most corners are shared between neighboring patches. The new implementation precomputes a `(latitudePatchCount + 1) × (longitudePatchCount + 1)` corner grid once per frame, cutting the sample call count by ~3.7× on `octopus3d3` and ~4× on `octopus3d2`.\n    -   Added per-frame longitude caching for `resolveContinuousTentacleInfluence`, `resolveContinuousLobeWave`, and `resolveLowerLobeWave` in the same two visuals. Each tentacle-influence evaluation runs an 8-iteration `Math.exp` loop over the seeded tentacle profiles, so calling it once per longitude grid value instead of once per corner cuts the dominant inner-loop cost by ~30×. The new `sampleContinuousOctopusSurfacePointWithLongitudeCache` / `sampleBlobbyOctopusSurfacePointWithLongitudeCache` helpers accept the cached values explicitly; the existing public sample functions are preserved for off-grid callers (eyes, mouth).\n\n-   Added `--wait [duration]` flag to `ptbk coder run` for controlling the delay between prompt rounds:\n\n    -   `--wait 1h` (or `--wait 30m`, `--wait 5s`, combinations like `--wait 1h30m`) waits the specified duration between rounds to avoid hitting harness rate limits. The first prompt executes immediately; the wait is inserted only before subsequent rounds.\n    -   `--wait` without a value retains the existing interactive behavior — waits for user confirmation before each prompt.\n    -   No flag (or `--no-wait`) means no waiting, which is now the default. `--no-wait` is kept for backward compatibility.\n\n-   Fixed `CliAgent` failing with `Missing --harness in non-dry run mode` when no `harness` is provided: `CliAgent` now falls back to the `PTBK_HARNESS` environment variable, mirroring `ptbk agent exec` behavior. Similarly falls back to `PTBK_MODEL` and `PTBK_THINKING_LEVEL` env vars. Extracted shared env-var constants (`PTBK_HARNESS_ENV`, `PTBK_MODEL_ENV`, `PTBK_THINKING_LEVEL_ENV`), harness names (`CLI_AGENT_HARNESS_NAMES`), and thinking-level values (`CLI_AGENT_THINKING_LEVEL_VALUES`) into the new `src/book-3.0/cliAgentEnv.ts` so CLI and library share a single source of truth. Fixed a pre-existing TypeScript error in `BookNodeAgentSource.ts` where `normalizeBookNodeAgentSource` did not accept the plain `string` allowed by its `book` option type.\n\n-   Fixed entity scanner false positive in `agentProjectPaths.ts` where the comment `// Re-export shared agent folder path constants...` caused the regex to match `export shared agent` and flag a missing `@private`/`@public` annotation; removed the misleading comment.\n\n-   Fixed `@promptbook/node` bundle so CLI-only `[🟡]` path constants no longer leak into the package: extracted shared agent-folder path constants (`AGENT_BOOK_FILE_PATH`, `AGENT_MESSAGES_DIRECTORY_PATH`, `AGENT_QUEUED_MESSAGES_DIRECTORY_PATH`, `AGENT_FINISHED_MESSAGES_DIRECTORY_PATH`, `AGENT_FAILED_MESSAGES_DIRECTORY_PATH`, `AGENT_PROJECTS_DIRECTORY_PATH`) into `src/book-3.0/agentFolderPaths.ts`, updated `agentProjectPaths.ts` to import and re-export from there, and updated `executeAgentChatTurn.ts` plus both agent-message prompt builders to import from the shared file instead of the CLI-only one. Added `[💞]` ignore note to `agentFolderPaths.ts` to suppress the file-name/entity-name discrepancy check.\n\n-   Optimized `CliAgent` to call the agent execution pipeline directly instead of spawning a `ptbk agent exec` child process, removing the intermediate CLI overhead while sharing the same `executeAgentChatTurn` logic used by the CLI command.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server chat pre-answers so the immediate placeholder response now focuses on confirming the job is being handled and avoids partial deliverables such as draft code or likely final-answer content.\n\n-   Optimized Agents Server agent/chat responsiveness by short-circuiting common local agent-route resolution, avoiding redundant active-chat refresh fetches while the live stream is healthy, reducing settled-chat reconciliation work during chat detail loads, and adding active chat job/timeout indexes for the hottest polling queries.\n\n-   Changed `ptbk agent chat` and `ptbk agent exec` console output so local harness stdout/stderr and the chat exit hint stay hidden by default and appear only with `--verbose`, leaving normal runs focused on the chat conversation or final answer.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server Sentry error-report tests so they assert the current Promptbook and Book version constants instead of stale hard-coded prerelease values.\n\n-   Added `CliAgent` and `LiteAgent` to `@promptbook/node` for running Book agents directly from Node.js:\n\n    -   `CliAgent` wraps `ptbk agent exec` through the existing Node command-execution utility, including in-memory Book source support by materializing temporary `.book` files when needed.\n    -   `LiteAgent` runs compiled Book agents through the OpenAI Agents SDK, reusing Promptbook system messages, prompt suffixes, tool definitions, and hosted knowledge support in a lighter in-process runtime.\n\n-   Added `ptbk agent chat` and `ptbk agent exec` for running a local `.book` agent directly from the CLI through the shared harness selection flags, including optional `--context` support and Promptbook-owned `.promptbook` scratch workspaces.\n\n-   Changed Promptbook CLI runner selection from `--agent` / `PTBK_AGENT` to `--harness` / `PTBK_HARNESS` across `ptbk coder run`, `ptbk agent-folder`, `ptbk agents-server start/dev`, standalone VPS runner setup, default scripts, and documentation.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server durable errors.\n\n-   Fixed standalone VPS Agents Server self-updates so Next.js `/_next/static` files are preserved across release handoffs, allowing open browser tabs to load previous hashed chunks instead  -   Non-interactive installs must now opt in explicitly with `PTBK_CONFIRM_FRESH_VPS=yes`, preventing automation from silently running on an already-configured server.\n\n-   Changed standalone VPS Agents Server installs so OpenAI Codex uses an existing ChatGPT login before falling back to `OPENAI_API_KEY` authentication.\n\n    -   Fixed the OpenAI Codex runner shell to source the installed Agents Server `.env` through `PTBK_AGENTS_SERVER_ENV_FILE`, detect `codex login status`, and keep `forced_login_method=chatgpt` when a ChatGPT account is active.\n    -   Fixed the ChatGPT-login login method (**ChatGPT account** vs. **API key**) on the completed coding-agent task status line next to the reused token-usage estimate, so task details show whether a run was billed to the server's ChatGPT subscription or the `OPENAI_API_KEY`.\n    -   Fixed the generated OpenAI Codex runner shell so Agents Server message folders can run outside a Git repository and prompt text cannot Agents Server domains backed by SQLite so numeric-looking metadata values, including `SERVER_NAME`, are read as strings instead of crashing the layout header with `split is not a function`.\n\n-   Changed standalone VPS Agents Server installs to default the coding runner to OpenAI Codex while keeping GitHub Copilot and the other runner choices available.\n\n-   Fixed standalone VPS Agents Agents Server, which rejected every management call and therefore never routed inbound or outbound agent mail:\n\n    -   Fixed `install.sh`, which decided that Stalwart was already bootstrapped whenever `/etc/stalwart/config.json` existed. Stalwart writes that file itself - it is only its storage descriptor, for example `{\"@type\":\"RocksDb\",\"path\":\"/var/lib/stalwart/\",...}` - already during its very first startup, long before anything is bootstrapped, and never touches it again. The installer therefore skipped the `x:Bootstrap/set` call on **every** fresh installation and left the mail server permanently in bootstrap mode, where it refuses every management call with `{\"type\":\"forbidden\",\"description\":\"The server is in bootstrap mode. ...\"}`. The bootstrap state is now read from Stalwart itself through a management probe, so a pending bootstrap is completed on the next installer run and an already bootstrapped server is left untouched.\n    -   Fixed the Stalwart management payloads, which sent JSON arrays for `aliases`, `credentials`, `memberGroupIds`, `stages`, and the MTA hook `enable.match` expression, while Stalwart serializes every `set` / `objectList` property as an object and answered `invalidPatch` / `Invalid value for object property`. Added shared `toStalwartJmapSet` and `toStalwartJmapObjectList` helpers so all payloads build these shapes in one place.\n    -   Fixed `install.sh`, which provisioned the Agents Server Stalwart administrator inside the reserved `promptbook.invalid` domain. Stalwart rejects such a domain as an `Invalid domain name`, so the step failed and, because of `set -Eeuo pipefail`, aborted the whole installation before nginx, firewall, and certificate configuration ever ran. The bootstrap-time administrator credentials are now kept as Stalwart's fixed `STALWART_RECOVERY_ADMIN` credentials instead of provisioning a second administrator account.\n    -   Fixed the Stalwart step of `install.sh` aborting the whole installation when the mail server cannot be bootstrapped. Because `configure_firewall`, `configure_nginx_reverse_proxy`, and `configure_ssl_certificates` all run afterwards, a mail server problem used to leave the VPS without a firewall, reverse proxy, or certificates. The step now warns and continues, and the bootstrap is retried by every later installer run.\n    -   Fixed outbound submission, which was configured for port `587`, a port a bootstrapped Stalwart never opens. Agents Server now submits through `submissions` on port `465` with implicit TLS, and the email server administration pages document that port instead of `587`.\n    -   Fixed the catch-all address being assigned before the mailbox behind it existed, so synchronizing an already-known domain no longer fails on its first management call.\n    -   Improved Stalwart error reporting so a rejected object now includes Stalwart's own `notCreated` / `notUpdated` reason, and a server still in **bootstrap mode** reports an actionable message instead of a raw `forbidden` response.\n    -   Fixed the `promptbook-agents-server` build, which loaded the Next.js command line interface through the hardcoded path `../../node_modules/next/dist/bin/next`. That path does not exist inside a git worktree without its own installed dependencies, such as the `ptbk coder --isolate` worktrees, so `npm run build` failed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` even though Next.js was resolvable. The new `apps/agents-server/scripts/next-cli.js` resolves it through Node's own module resolution instead.\n\n-   Fixed the self-contained Stalwart mail server staying unusable whenever its initial setup was left pending. Completing that setup used to be the sole responsibility of `install.sh`, so a mail server which was installed before the bootstrap fix - or whose bootstrap failed once - answered every management call with `{\"type\":\"forbidden\",\"description\":\"The server is in bootstrap mode. ...\"}`, and **Synchronize Stalwart** on `/admin/email-server` could only report the error, never resolve it. Because the VPS self-update runs the _deployed_ release's installer, such a server stayed broken for at least one more update cycle. Agents Server now completes the bootstrap itself as the first step of every domain synchronization, which happens on startup and on **Synchronize Stalwart**, and it asks Stalwart for its bootstrap state instead of inferring it from files on disk. The setup Stalwart receives - mail hostname, default domain, automatic DKIM keys, and no ACME certificate request because nginx and certbot own every certificate on the VPS - is now defined by `buildStalwartBootstrapValue`, which `install.sh` mirrors under the shared `[📬]` marker because a fresh VPS is bootstrapped before Agents Server is built, and the result is verified against Stalwart itself so a bootstrap that was accepted but not applied is reported with the remaining manual step instead of a raw `forbidden` response. The installer keeps performing the bootstrap for a fresh installation and additionally waits until Stalwart really left bootstrap mode after the restart it needs to open its mail listeners, so the first synchronization of a newly started Agents Server no longer races a mail server that is still coming up.\n-   Improved the Agents Server **Book language manual** so its linked table of contents navigates directly to each commitment, and each end-to-end example links its used commitments back to their sections. The manual now describes `@Foo` and `{Foo foo}` as agent references rather than parameters, renames the `---` primitive to **Multiple agent**, documents code fences as ` ``` `, links every generated-from source to the Promptbook repository, hides parser/runtime implementation details and unfinished commitments, and keeps each commitment example focused on its canonical keyword with only `GOAL` and `CLOSED` as supporting syntax.\n\n-   Fixed the published `@promptbook/components` package, which broke the production build of every browser application that installs `ptbk`, `promptbook` or `@promptbook/components`. Rendered markdown is sanitized by `DOMPurify`, which needs a DOM, so `renderMarkdown` creates one through `jsdom` whenever it runs outside of a browser - for example during server-side rendering. That code path is unreachable in a browser, but bundlers resolve `require('jsdom')` statically, so `next build` followed it into `jsdom` and failed with **Module not found: Can't resolve `fs`** together with the same error for `child_process` and `net`. It failed even for an application that imports `<MarkdownContent/>` with `ssr: false`, because a bundler resolves a module it will never execute just as eagerly as one it will:\n\n    -   The generated manifest of every package that is not Node-only now declares `\"browser\": { \"jsdom\": false }`, which is the standard way to tell a browser bundler to replace a Node-only dependency with an empty module. Browser builds therefore no longer follow `jsdom` (and no longer ship it), while Node.js ignores the `browser` field and keeps resolving the real library for server-side rendering. The stubs are derived from the dependencies which the generated package really has, so a Node-only dependency which appears in a browser-facing package in the future is covered without another manual change.\n    -   Creating the server-side DOM moved from `renderMarkdown` into `$provideServerDomWindow`, which is now the single place where browser-facing code touches `jsdom`. A runtime that can provide neither the DOM of a browser nor `jsdom` is now reported as a branded `EnvironmentMismatchError` explaining why markdown can not be sanitized, instead of failing with `JSDOM is not a constructor`.\n    -   The list of Node-only packages is now shared through `isNodeOnlyPackage` between the publish-safety check and the dependency step of the package generation, instead of being written down twice.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":3,"newStart":1,"newLines":41,"lines":["+-   Fixed the warnings printed while installing `ptbk`. The 62 you saw = these 48 plus 14 `@promptbook/*` rows npm adds for depending on them. Fixed by raising pins that advisories named: `next` 15.4.11→15.5.25 (also kills `sharp`), `express`→4.22.3 (`body-parser`/`qs`/`path-to-regexp`), `socket.io-client`→4.8.3 (`ws`/`engine.io-client`), `mailparser`→3.9.20 (`linkify-it` + nested `nodemailer`), `@aws-sdk/client-s3`→3.1134.0 (`fast-xml-parser`), `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`→1.26.0, `nodemailer`→^9.1.1, `dompurify`→3.4.15, `jspdf`→4.2.1, `postcss`→8.5.28.\n\nTwo notes on judgment calls I made, since they're the ones worth disagreeing with:\n- **`nodemailer` 7 → 9 crosses majors.** I did it anyway because the only API used is `createTransport`/`sendMail` (one file), it keeps Node 18 support, and it dedupes with what `mailparser` now installs. Say the word and I'll revert it to `^7`.\n- **I skipped `monaco-editor` 0.54 → 0.56.** It only moves one advisory from moderate to low — its bundled `dompurify@3.4.8` stays vulnerable either way — and nothing in the suite exercises the Book editor.\n\nLeft deliberately unfixed (all documented in the changelog): `showdown` and `xlsx`/`markitdown-ts` have no fixed release at all; `@ai-sdk/*`, `undici` and `@vercel/blob` need majors that require Node 22; `localtunnel` has no release without a vulnerable `axios`; `next`'s residual moderate + its bundled `postcss` need Next 16.\n\nVerified green so far: `test-name-discrepancies`, `test-spellcheck`, `test-lint`, `test-types`, `test-package-generation`, `test-unit` (765 suites / 3400 tests), agents-server `lint`. -   Keep in mind the DRY _(don't repeat yourself)_ principle.
-   Do a proper analysis of the current functionality before you start implementing.
-   Add the changes into the [changelog](changelog/_current-preversion.md)

## Your Behavior

You are Promptbook Developer
You are a helpful, honest, and intelligent AI assistant. Your goal is to provide accurate, clear, and concise responses while being friendly and engaging. Think step-by-step before answering complex questions.

### Rules

-   If you're unsure about something, say so and offer to look it up or clarify.
-   You can use Markdown formatting in the messages like **bold** or *italic*
-   You can use Markdown code blocks if needed

For example:

```javascript
console.log('Hello');
```
-   Keep in mind the DRY _(don't repeat yourself)_ principle.
-   Keep in mind the SOLID principles.
-   Do a proper analysis of the current functionality before you start implementing.
-   Keep small responsibilities of functions and classes, avoid creating big functions or classes that do many things.
-   When throwing errors, throw [branded errors](src/errors) and use `spaceTrim` utility to write clear and well-formatted multiline detailed error messages.

Output Format: errors as markdown, for example `variables` should be in backticks and important notes can be in bold.
-   Constants should always be `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`.
-   Boolean variables should always be prefixed with `is`, for example `isUserChatJobLeaseExpired` or `IS_DEBUG_MODE`.
-   Do not use abbreviations, for example use `isExpired` instead of `isExp`, `translateMessage` instead of `t`, etc.
It is fine to use well-known abbreviations, for example `id`, `url`, `html`, etc.
-   When writing multiline strings, use `spaceTrim` utility.
-   Do only the change described in the prompt. Do not add any additional features or make any additional changes that are not described there.
If you find some critical issue that is not described in the prompt, report it to `agents-messages` in the root of the project.

### Prompt suffix
-   If you're unsure about something, say so and offer to look it up or clarify.
-   You can use Markdown formatting in the messages like **bold** or *italic*
-   You can use Markdown code blocks if needed

For example:

```javascript
console.log('Hello');
```
-   Keep in mind the DRY _(don't repeat yourself)_ principle.
-   Keep in mind the SOLID principles.
-   Do a proper analysis of the current functionality before you start implementing.
-   Keep small responsibilities of functions and classes, avoid creating big functions or classes that do many things.
-   When throwing errors, throw [branded errors](src/errors) and use `spaceTrim` utility to write clear and well-formatted multiline detailed error messages.
-   Constants should always be `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`.
-   Boolean variables should always be prefixed with `is`, for example `isUserChatJobLeaseExpired` or `IS_DEBUG_MODE`.
-   Do not use abbreviations, for example use `isExpired` instead of `isExp`, `translateMessage` instead of `t`, etc.
It is fine to use well-known abbreviations, for example `id`, `url`, `html`, etc.
-   When writing multiline strings, use `spaceTrim` utility.
-   Do only the change described in the prompt. Do not add any additional features or make any additional changes that are not described there.
If you find some critical issue that is not described in the prompt, report it to `agents-messages` in the root of the project.

## Context

### How to Contribute

-   **Add changes in [Changelog](/changelog/_current-preversion.md)**
-   **Test your changes** to ensure they work as expected, use `npm test`

### Code Style

-   Follow the existing code style and structure.
-   Use comments to explain complex logic.

### Emoji in `[brackets]`

-   `[any emoji]` Connects multiple places that are related to each other across the repository
-   `[number]` Connects multiple places that are related to each other across the file
-   `[🧠]` Marks a place where there is something to decide and think about.
-   `[🕕]` List of models _(that should be progresively updated)_
    -   Prompt: Update available models and their prices, search online
-   `[🔼]` Marks an entity (function, class, type,...) in other project (like Promptbook.studio) which should be moved to this repository
-   `[🚉]` Marks an types / interfaces / structures fully serializable as JSON, not marking `string_` and `number_` prefixed aliases
-   `[🧹]` Need to implement garbage collection
-   `[🐣]` Easter eggs
-   `[💩]` Shitty code that needs refactoring
-   `$` When entity (function, class) starts by `$`, it means it is not pure and can have side effects.
-   3x `!` Marks a place that needs to be fixed before releasing a pre-release version.
-   4x (and more) `!` Marks a place that needs to be fixed as soon as possible.
-   `@@@` Marks a place where text / documentation / ... must be written.
-   [⚫] Code in this file should never be published in any package
-   [🟢] Code in this file should never be published into packages that could be imported into browser environment
-   [🔵] Code in this file should never be published outside of `@promptbook/browser`
-   [🟡] Code in this file should never be published outside of `@promptbook/cli`
-   [💞] Ignore a discrepancy between file name and entity name

### Generated code

Across the repository, there are several places where code has been generated automatically.
Do not edit these places manually, as they will be overwritten by the code generation process. Edit the source files instead.

> ⚠️ WARNING: This code has been generated so that any manual changes will be overwritten

### Dictionary

-   **Promptbook Engine vs. Agent Server** sre two distinct parts you should know the difference:
    -   **Promptbook Engine** is the core engine that powers AI agents, it is located in `/src` folder. It is framework-agnostic and can be used in different applications. It can run as standalone javascript/typescript library, CLI environment, or be integrated into different applications. It can be also runned in Agent Server:
    -   **Agent Server** is a specific application that uses the Promptbook Engine to provide a web and API interface for creating and interacting with AI agents. It is located in `/apps/agents-server` folder.
-   **Commitments** are basic syntax elements that add specific functionalities to AI agents
    -   They are used in `agentSource`, there are commitments like `PERSONA`, `RULE`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE CALENDAR`, `USE PROJECT`, `META IMAGE`, etc.
    -   Commitments are in the folder `/src/commitments`
    -   Each commitment starts with a keyword, e.g., `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE PROJECT`, etc. on a begining of the line and end by new co
    -   Agent source with commitments is parsed by two functions:
        -   `parseAgentSource` which is a lightweight parser for agent source, it parses basic information and its purpose is to be quick and synchronous. The commitments there are hardcoded.
        -   `createAgentModelRequirements` which is an asynchronous function that creates model requirements it applies each commitment one by one and works asynchronously.

### Common rules

-   Always analyze the context and requirements before generating any code.
-   Write clear, maintainable, and well-documented code.
-   Write JSDoc comments for all entities - functions, classes, types, top-level constants, etc.
    -   When this entity is exported from the file and it is under `src` folder _(not for example in the `apps` folder)_, it must be marked either as `@public` or `@private` at the end of the JSDoc comment.
    -   For example: "@private internal utility of <Chat/>" / "@public exported from `@promptbook/browser`"
    -   If you don't know, prefer to mark it as private, we can always change it to public later, but changing from public to private may cause breaking changes.
-   You (the AI coding agent) are running inside a Node process, so do not kill all Node processes such as `taskkill /F /IM node.exe`. If you need to stop something you spawned, kill only that specific process, for example by PID or by port.

### Additional context

-   Look at attached images if there are present
-   Attached images are in folder `prompts` on the root of the project
    -   For example the ![alt text](screenshots/foo.png) is image file `prompts/screenshots/foo.png`

#### Agents server installed on VPS _(as additional context)_

-   There are two distinct things:
    1. Entire VPS
    2. Each server
-   On one VPS there can be multiple servers and each server has its own domain
-   Most things (like agents, projects, metadata, etc.) are living on each server and some things (like environment variables, superadmin, etc.) are bound to entire VPS
-   Purpose of this is to be able to run multiple clients on one VPS and each client can have its own server with its own domain and settings
-   The entire VPS is managed by superadmin and each server is managed by normal admin of that server _(or superadmin can also manage each server)_
-   Superadmin has always name `admin` and password hardcoded in environment variable `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
-   The VPS is installed by running [the `install.sh`](install.sh) script on a fresh VPS
-   Servers can be added and removed by superadmin on `/superadmin/servers` page

#### The Agents Server menu _(as additional context)_

The menu of the agent server looks like this:

1. The navigation hierarchy
    - Icon and Server name _(for example Promptbook Agents Server)_
    - arrow ">" and Agents or picked agent name (organized in folders)
    - arrow ">" and the view Profile / Chat / Book of the agent or nothing if no agent is picked
2. The menu items
    - Documentation
    - System
3. Control panel and user menu
    - Control panel
    - User menu with the avatar and the name of the user

#### Database migrations for Agents server _(as additional context)_

-   Migrations are located in `apps/agents-server/src/database/migrations`
-   Be aware that table names in migrations have prefix `prefix_` _(look at existing migrations for reference)_
-   Migrations should be backwards compatible:
    -   Meaning that earlier versions of the server should be able to run with the database after migration without any issues.
    -   This is important because we want to have the same database for production and preview environments.
    -   This database will be migrated to the latest version of the preview environment, but the production environment should be able to run with it without any issues.
    -   The only thing that can happen is that older versions of the server will not be able to use new features.
    -   Adding new columns, tables, etc. is fine, but do not remove or rename existing ones, and do not change the meaning of existing columns or tables.
    -   When in doubt, prefer to add new things instead of changing existing ones.

#### Metadata of Agents server _(as additional context)_

-   There is a table called `Metadata`.
-   It has `key` and `value` fields.
-   It is a similar concept to configuration, but this configuration can be changed by administrators in the Agents Server website.

#### Book Language blueprint _(as additional context)_

Book language is a domain-specific language used for defining AI agents in the Promptbook Engine and Agents server.
It has lightweight syntax and keywords (the commitments) that allow you to define the "soul" of the agent.
The book language is designed to be human-readable and easy to write, while also being powerful enough to express complex agent behaviors.

Every agent has its source defined in the book language, which is called "agent source". The agent source is parsed and processed by the Promptbook Engine to create the actual AI agent that can interact with users and perform tasks.
This agent source is internally converted to a structured format called "agent model requirements" which are the actual raw technical instructions for the AI model to run the agent.

There is a standalone book language documentation on each agent server on `/api/docs/book.md` route, for example `https://live.ptbk.io/api/docs/book-language.md?language=en`.
Use it as a reference for the syntax and semantics of the book language, and modify `apps/agents-server/src/utils/bookLanguageDocumentation/createStandaloneBookLanguageMarkdown.ts` if it is relevant to the change you are doing.

##### Commitments _(as additional context and part of Book Language)_

Commitments are basic syntax elements that add specific functionalities to AI agents written in `book` language.

-   They are used in `agentSource`, there are commitments like `PERSONA`, `RULE`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE CALENDAR`, `USE PROJECT`, `META IMAGE`, `CLOSED`, etc.
-   They are in the folder `src/commitments`.
-   Each commitment starts with a keyword, e.g. `PERSONA`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE PROJECT`, etc. on a beginning of the line and ends by a new commitment or the end of the book.
-   There is a general pattern that the commitment keyword is followed by a space and then by the content of the commitment, for example:
    -   `PERSONA You are a helpful assistant that helps with cooking recipes.`
    -   `USE MCP https://mcp.example.com/server`
-   In the commitment context, you can reference external agents, for example:
    -   `TEAM You can talk to {Criminal lawyer} and {Financial advisor}`

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UmuSJF5aENxaQV8f6Kkuuv","type":"tool_result","content":"<system-reminder>This memory is 5 days old. Verify against current code before asserting as fact.</system-reminder>\n1\t---\n2\tname: ptbk-install-peer-warnings-task\n3\tdescription: \"\\\"[✨👉] When installing ptbk there are lot of peer dependency warnings\\\" — the zod 3 vs zod 4 split, why @promptbook/cli cannot just drop zod, and the fast --package-lock-only way to reproduce npm ERESOLVE\"\n4\tmetadata: \n5\t  node_type: memory\n6\t  type: project\n7\t  originSessionId: ae9faf42-babf-481b-a708-5164f847cb92\n8\t  modified: 2026-09-11T16:15:51.414Z\n9\t---\n10\t\n11\tFixed 2026-09-11. `npm i ptbk` printed 13 `ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` events; 10 of them were zod.\n12\t\n13\t**Root cause (two independent parts):**\n14\t1. The tree contained two irreconcilable zod families — `@ai-sdk/openai@1` / `@ai-sdk/google@1` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@0` peer-require `zod@^3.0.0` (every version of those majors does), while `@openai/agents` peer-requires `zod@^4.0.0` and the Agents Server itself imports zod 4. No single hoisted zod satisfies both. Fixed by upgrading to `@ai-sdk/openai@2.0.127` / `@ai-sdk/google@2.0.97` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@1.0.56` (peer `^3.25.76 || ^4.1.8`).\n15\t2. `bundleReferencesDependency` in `scripts/generate-packages/addDependenciesForGeneratedPackages.ts` substring-matched `from 'x'` anywhere in `packages/*/esm/index.es.js`, so the **code templates inside the transpilers** (`AgentOsTranspiler`, `AnthropicClaudeManagedTranspiler` emit `import { z } from 'zod';` for the *transpiled* project) made `@promptbook/core` publish `zod`, `dotenv` and `@anthropic-ai/sdk` as real dependencies. Fixed by requiring `import`/`export` needles to sit on a line that *starts* with the keyword (rollup always emits real imports at column 0); `require(`/`import(` calls still match anywhere.\n16\t\n17\t**Why:** these traps are invisible from the code — the `zod` pin looks deliberate, and the obvious \"just drop zod from `@promptbook/cli`\" is wrong.\n18\t\n19\t**How to apply:**\n20\t- **Do not** try to remove `zod` (or any root dependency) from `@promptbook/cli`: `rollup.config.js` gives the cli `additionalDependencies: [..., ...Object.keys(dependencies)]`, i.e. *all* root deps, because the cli ships `apps/agents-server` and that app imports zod (`managementApiSchemas.ts`, MCP route). The cli must keep it.\n21\t- **Do not** jump to the newest `@ai-sdk/*`: `@ai-sdk/openai@4` / `google@4` / `deepseek@3` (and `@ai-sdk/provider-utils@5`) declare `engines: node >=22`, which would break the repo's `engines: node >=18.18.0`. The `2.x`/`1.x` line accepts zod 4 and still says `node >=18`.\n22\t- Upgrading past `@ai-sdk/*@1` forces a `LanguageModelV1 → V2` migration of `src/llm-providers/vercel/createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider.ts` (used by Google **and** Deepseek): `provider.chat(modelId)` takes no settings, `doGenerate` loses `inputFormat`/`mode`, the result is `content: Array<{type,...}>` instead of `text`, and usage is `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`. `npm run test-types` verifies all of it because the request is typed `Parameters<typeof model.doGenerate>[0]`.\n23\t- **Reproduce/verify npm warnings in ~1 min instead of ~8:** `npm install ptbk@<version> --package-lock-only --no-audit --no-fund` in a scratch dir — registry metadata only, no tarballs, identical ERESOLVE output. To test a *candidate* manifest, write the generated `packages/cli/package.json` `dependencies` into a local `file:` package and resolve that.\n24\t- Compute the exact conflict list from the lockfile: walk `packages[*].peerDependencies`, resolve each peer by climbing `node_modules` segments, `semver.satisfies(..., {loose: true})` — **`loose` matters**, `@tailwindcss/typography` has an invalid range (`>=3.0.0 || insiders || ...`) that is a false positive without it.\n25\t- 3 warnings are unfixable from here: `swagger-ui-react`'s nested `react-copy-to-clipboard` / `react-debounce-input` / `react-inspector` cap React at 18 and are unmaintained. `swagger-ui-react` is really used (`apps/agents-server/src/app/swagger/SwaggerPageClient.tsx`).\n26\t- `@promptbook/cli` also exposed a separate defect worth knowing: `createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider` calls `model.doGenerate(rawRequest)` **twice** per prompt (double cost, half-counted usage) — reported in `agents-messages/2026-09-1100-vercel-adapter-calls-the-model-twice.message.md`, deliberately not fixed.\n27\t\n28\tRelated: [[ptbk-browser-bundle-jsdom-task]] (same generator, `browser` field), [[promptbook-verification-step-order]]\n29\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"56de9054-2782-4457-ba7c-c675f80fa1a3","uuid":"b29e4f4e-db0d-4bba-bba9-9f645d544109","timestamp":"2026-09-17T12:07:56.239Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\.claude\\projects\\C--Users-me-work-ai-promptbook\\memory\\ptbk-install-peer-warnings-task.md","content":"---\nname: 2026-09-11T16:15:51.414Z\n---\n\nFixed 2026-09-11. `npm i ptbk` printed 13 `ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` events; 10 of them were zod.\n\n**Root cause (two independent parts):**\n1. The tree contained two irreconcilable zod families — `@ai-sdk/openai@1` / `@ai-sdk/google@1` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@0` peer-require `zod@^3.0.0` (every version of those majors does), while `@openai/agents` peer-requires `zod@^4.0.0` and the Agents Server itself imports zod 4. No single hoisted zod satisfies both. Fixed by upgrading to `@ai-sdk/openai@2.0.127` / `@ai-sdk/google@2.0.97` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@1.0.56` (peer `^3.25.76 || ^4.1.8`).\n2. `bundleReferencesDependency` in `scripts/generate-packages/addDependenciesForGeneratedPackages.ts` substring-matched `from 'x'` anywhere in `packages/*/esm/index.es.js`, so the **code templates inside the transpilers** (`AgentOsTranspiler`, `AnthropicClaudeManagedTranspiler` emit `import { z } from 'zod';` for the *transpiled* project) made `@promptbook/core` publish `zod`, `dotenv` and `@anthropic-ai/sdk` as real dependencies. Fixed by requiring `import`/`export` needles to sit on a line that *starts* with the keyword (rollup always emits real imports at column 0); `require(`/`import(` calls still match anywhere.\n\n**Why:** these traps are invisible from the code — the `zod` pin looks deliberate, and the obvious \"just drop zod from `@promptbook/cli`\" is wrong.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- **Do not** try to remove `zod` (or any root dependency) from `@promptbook/cli`: `rollup.config.js` gives the cli `additionalDependencies: [..., ...Object.keys(dependencies)]`, i.e. *all* root deps, because the cli ships `apps/agents-server` and that app imports zod (`managementApiSchemas.ts`, MCP route). The cli must keep it.\n- **Do not** jump to the newest `@ai-sdk/*`: `@ai-sdk/openai@4` / `google@4` / `deepseek@3` (and `@ai-sdk/provider-utils@5`) declare `engines: node >=22`, which would break the repo's `engines: node >=18.18.0`. The `2.x`/`1.x` line accepts zod 4 and still says `node >=18`.\n- Upgrading past `@ai-sdk/*@1` forces a `LanguageModelV1 → V2` migration of `src/llm-providers/vercel/createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider.ts` (used by Google **and** Deepseek): `provider.chat(modelId)` takes no settings, `doGenerate` loses `inputFormat`/`mode`, the result is `content: Array<{type,...}>` instead of `text`, and usage is `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`. `npm run test-types` verifies all of it because the request is typed `Parameters<typeof model.doGenerate>[0]`.\n- **Reproduce/verify npm warnings in ~1 min instead of ~8:** `npm install ptbk@<version> --package-lock-only --no-audit --no-fund` in a scratch dir — registry metadata only, no tarballs, identical ERESOLVE output. To test a *candidate* manifest, write the generated `packages/cli/package.json` `dependencies` into a local `file:` package and resolve that.\n- Compute the exact conflict list from the lockfile: walk `packages[*].peerDependencies`, resolve each peer by climbing `node_modules` segments, `semver.satisfies(..., {loose: true})` — **`loose` matters**, `@tailwindcss/typography` has an invalid range (`>=3.0.0 || insiders || ...`) that is a false positive without it.\n- 3 warnings are unfixable from here: `swagger-ui-react`'s nested `react-copy-to-clipboard` / `react-debounce-input` / `react-inspector` cap React at 18 and are unmaintained. `swagger-ui-react` is really used (`apps/agents-server/src/app/swagger/SwaggerPageClient.tsx`).\n- `@promptbook/cli` also exposed a separate defect worth knowing: `createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider` calls `model.doGenerate(rawRequest)` **twice** per prompt (double cost, half-counted usage) — reported in `agents-messages/2026-09-1100-vercel-adapter-calls-the-model-twice.message.md`, deliberately not fixed.\n\nRelated: [[ptbk-browser-bundle-jsdom-task]] (same generator, `browser` field), [[promptbook-verification-step-order]]\n","numLines":29,"startLine":1,"totalLines":29}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Cv9RkXbNpHonC6PkqoJRcy","type":"tool_result","content":"diff --git a/changelog/_current-preversion.md b/changelog/_current-preversion.md\nindex 695a46a90..eeb5889f1 100644\n--- a/changelog/_current-preversion.md\n+++ b/changelog/_current-preversion.md\n@@ -1,3 +1,41 @@\n+-   Fixed the warnings printed while installing `ptbk`. Five of the ten `npm warn deprecated` lines were caused by\n+    Promptbook itself and are gone, and an installation resolves 96 packages fewer than before:\n+\n+    -   `crypto` was declared as a dependency, although the package of that name is only a deprecated placeholder for\n+        the Node.js built-in module. Node.js resolves `crypto` to its built-in module in every case, so the package was\n+        downloaded and warned about without ever being used by anything.\n+    -   `y-websocket-server` was declared as a dependency without being imported anywhere. The only thing which runs\n+        it, `other/y-websocket-server/y-websocket.js`, starts it through `npx`, which resolves it on its own.\n+    -   `glob-promise` is replaced by `glob` itself, which returns promises since its version 9 and no longer needs a\n+        wrapper. `glob-promise` holds `glob` at version 8, which still depends on the deprecated `inflight`, so those\n+        two warned together. All eleven call sites now go through one `findFilesByGlob` utility, which keeps the two\n+        things `glob` version 8 guaranteed and the current one does not - `/` separators on Windows and a stable\n+        alphabetical order - so nothing which reads the matched filenames had to change.\n+    -   `express-openapi-validator` is updated to a release which uses `multer` 2 instead of the deprecated `multer` 1.\n+\n+    The five remaining deprecation warnings cannot be resolved from this repository. `lodash.get` and\n+    `whatwg-encoding` are used by the newest `express-openapi-validator` and `jsdom` as well, `prebuild-install` is a\n+    dependency of `better-sqlite3` which only its version 13 drops - and that version requires Node.js 22, while\n+    Promptbook still supports Node.js 18 - and `crypto-js` and `@azure/openai` are deprecated by their authors but\n+    really used by Promptbook.\n+\n+-   Reduced what `npm audit` reports after installing `ptbk` from 48 vulnerable packages to 15, and from 3 critical\n+    advisories to none. Every version pinned by Promptbook which an advisory named is raised to a release without that\n+    advisory: `next` (which also carried the only critical advisories and brings its bundled `sharp` with it),\n+    `express` (with `body-parser`, `qs` and `path-to-regexp`), `socket.io-client` (with `engine.io-client` and `ws`),\n+    `mailparser` (with `linkify-it` and its own `nodemailer`), `@aws-sdk/client-s3` (with `fast-xml-parser`),\n+    `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `nodemailer`, `dompurify`, `jspdf` and `postcss`. None of these upgrades changes the\n+    Node.js versions Promptbook supports. `nodemailer` is the only one which crosses a major version, from 7 to 9,\n+    and Promptbook calls only its `createTransport` and `sendMail`, which those versions do not change - it is now\n+    also the same installation which `mailparser` uses.\n+\n+    What is still reported either has no fixed release at all - `showdown`, and `xlsx` inside `markitdown-ts` - or can\n+    only be fixed by an upgrade which would break something else: the fixed majors of `@ai-sdk/openai`,\n+    `@ai-sdk/google`, `@ai-sdk/deepseek` (together with `undici`) and `@vercel/blob` require Node.js 22, `localtunnel`\n+    has no release which stops using a vulnerable `axios`, and a moderate advisory on `next` with a high one on the\n+    `postcss` bundled inside it, plus `monaco-editor` with the `dompurify` bundled inside it, are only fixed by\n+    upgrades of Next.js and the Monaco editor which deserve their own change.\n+\n -   `ptbk coder` now resolves `FROM`, `IMPORT`, and `TEAM` references across local agent books before compiling coding\n     instructions. Names in `@Name` and `{Name}` match first-line book titles discovered recursively beneath the selected\n     agent's folder. `./` and `../` paths resolve from the declaring book, other paths from the working directory, and\n=== prompts diff ===\ndiff --git a/prompts/2026-09-0151-ptbk-fix-install-warnings.md b/prompts/2026-09-0151-ptbk-fix-install-warnings.md\nindex f724559f2..db9278cf9 100644\n--- a/prompts/2026-09-0151-ptbk-fix-install-warnings.md\n+++ b/prompts/2026-09-0151-ptbk-fix-install-warnings.md\n@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@\n-[ ]\n+[^] (2 attempts) by Promptbook Developer on Claude Code `claude-opus-5` thinking `max` - Implementation 6.81 39 minutes; Testing 21 minutes; Fixing in progress\n \n [✨👉] When installing `ptbk` there are lot of peer dependency warnings, fix it\n \n@@ -477,3 +477,4 @@ $\n -   Keep in mind the DRY _(don't repeat yourself)_ principle.\n -   Do a proper analysis of the current functionality before you start implementing.\n -   Add the changes into the [changelog](changelog/_current-preversion.md)\n+","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"56de9054-2782-4457-ba7c-c675f80fa1a3","uuid":"3f88d136-f1a7-45dc-80c5-80d8c70e0a44","timestamp":"2026-09-17T12:09:12.164Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"diff --git a/changelog/_current-preversion.md b/changelog/_current-preversion.md\nindex 695a46a90..eeb5889f1 100644\n--- a/changelog/_current-preversion.md\n+++ b/changelog/_current-preversion.md\n@@ -1,3 +1,41 @@\n+-   Fixed the warnings printed while installing `ptbk`. ## Your Behavior

You are Promptbook Developer
You are a helpful, honest, and intelligent AI assistant. Your goal is to provide accurate, clear, and concise responses while being friendly and engaging. Think step-by-step before answering complex questions.

### Rules

-   If you're unsure about something, say so and offer to look it up or clarify.
-   You can use Markdown formatting in the messages like **bold** or *italic*
-   You can use Markdown code blocks if needed

For example:

```javascript
console.log('Hello');
```
-   Keep in mind the DRY _(don't repeat yourself)_ principle.
-   Keep in mind the SOLID principles.
-   Do a proper analysis of the current functionality before you start implementing.
-   Keep small responsibilities of functions and classes, avoid creating big functions or classes that do many things.
-   When throwing errors, throw [branded errors](src/errors) and use `spaceTrim` utility to write clear and well-formatted multiline detailed error messages.

Output Format: errors as markdown, for example `variables` should be in backticks and important notes can be in bold.
-   Constants should always be `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`.
-   Boolean variables should always be prefixed with `is`, for example `isUserChatJobLeaseExpired` or `IS_DEBUG_MODE`.
-   Do not use abbreviations, for example use `isExpired` instead of `isExp`, `translateMessage` instead of `t`, etc.
It is fine to use well-known abbreviations, for example `id`, `url`, `html`, etc.
-   When writing multiline strings, use `spaceTrim` utility.
-   Do only the change described in the prompt. Do not add any additional features or make any additional changes that are not described there.
If you find some critical issue that is not described in the prompt, report it to `agents-messages` in the root of the project.

## Context

### How to Contribute

-   **Add changes in [Changelog](/changelog/_current-preversion.md)**
-   **Test your changes** to ensure they work as expected, use `npm test`

### Code Style

-   Follow the existing code style and structure.
-   Use comments to explain complex logic.

### Emoji in `[brackets]`

-   `[any emoji]` Connects multiple places that are related to each other across the repository
-   `[number]` Connects multiple places that are related to each other across the file
-   `[🧠]` Marks a place where there is something to decide and think about.
-   `[🕕]` List of models _(that should be progresively updated)_
    -   Prompt: Update available models and their prices, search online
-   `[🔼]` Marks an entity (function, class, type,...) in other project (like Promptbook.studio) which should be moved to this repository
-   `[🚉]` Marks an types / interfaces / structures fully serializable as JSON, not marking `string_` and `number_` prefixed aliases
-   `[🧹]` Need to implement garbage collection
-   `[🐣]` Easter eggs
-   `[💩]` Shitty code that needs refactoring
-   `$` When entity (function, class) starts by `$`, it means it is not pure and can have side effects.
-   3x `!` Marks a place that needs to be fixed before releasing a pre-release version.
-   4x (and more) `!` Marks a place that needs to be fixed as soon as possible.
-   `@@@` Marks a place where text / documentation / ... must be written.
-   [⚫] Code in this file should never be published in any package
-   [🟢] Code in this file should never be published into packages that could be imported into browser environment
-   [🔵] Code in this file should never be published outside of `@promptbook/browser`
-   [🟡] Code in this file should never be published outside of `@promptbook/cli`
-   [💞] Ignore a discrepancy between file name and entity name

### Generated code

Across the repository, there are several places where code has been generated automatically.
Do not edit these places manually, as they will be overwritten by the code generation process. Edit the source files instead.

> ⚠️ WARNING: This code has been generated so that any manual changes will be overwritten

### Dictionary

-   **Promptbook Engine vs. Agent Server** sre two distinct parts you should know the difference:
    -   **Promptbook Engine** is the core engine that powers AI agents, it is located in `/src` folder. It is framework-agnostic and can be used in different applications. It can run as standalone javascript/typescript library, CLI environment, or be integrated into different applications. It can be also runned in Agent Server:
    -   **Agent Server** is a specific application that uses the Promptbook Engine to provide a web and API interface for creating and interacting with AI agents. It is located in `/apps/agents-server` folder.
-   **Commitments** are basic syntax elements that add specific functionalities to AI agents
    -   They are used in `agentSource`, there are commitments like `PERSONA`, `RULE`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE CALENDAR`, `USE PROJECT`, `META IMAGE`, etc.
    -   Commitments are in the folder `/src/commitments`
    -   Each commitment starts with a keyword, e.g., `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE PROJECT`, etc. on a begining of the line and end by new co
    -   Agent source with commitments is parsed by two functions:
        -   `parseAgentSource` which is a lightweight parser for agent source, it parses basic information and its purpose is to be quick and synchronous. The commitments there are hardcoded.
        -   `createAgentModelRequirements` which is an asynchronous function that creates model requirements it applies each commitment one by one and works asynchronously.

### Common rules

-   Always analyze the context and requirements before generating any code.
-   Write clear, maintainable, and well-documented code.
-   Write JSDoc comments for all entities - functions, classes, types, top-level constants, etc.
    -   When this entity is exported from the file and it is under `src` folder _(not for example in the `apps` folder)_, it must be marked either as `@public` or `@private` at the end of the JSDoc comment.
    -   For example: "@private internal utility of <Chat/>" / "@public exported from `@promptbook/browser`"
    -   If you don't know, prefer to mark it as private, we can always change it to public later, but changing from public to private may cause breaking changes.
-   You (the AI coding agent) are running inside a Node process, so do not kill all Node processes such as `taskkill /F /IM node.exe`. If you need to stop something you spawned, kill only that specific process, for example by PID or by port.

### Additional context

-   Look at attached images if there are present
-   Attached images are in folder `prompts` on the root of the project
    -   For example the ![alt text](screenshots/foo.png) is image file `prompts/screenshots/foo.png`

#### Agents server installed on VPS _(as additional context)_

-   There are two distinct things:
    1. Entire VPS
    2. Each server
-   On one VPS there can be multiple servers and each server has its own domain
-   Most things (like agents, projects, metadata, etc.) are living on each server and some things (like environment variables, superadmin, etc.) are bound to entire VPS
-   Purpose of this is to be able to run multiple clients on one VPS and each client can have its own server with its own domain and settings
-   The entire VPS is managed by superadmin and each server is managed by normal admin of that server _(or superadmin can also manage each server)_
-   Superadmin has always name `admin` and password hardcoded in environment variable `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
-   The VPS is installed by running [the `install.sh`](install.sh) script on a fresh VPS
-   Servers can be added and removed by superadmin on `/superadmin/servers` page

#### The Agents Server menu _(as additional context)_

The menu of the agent server looks like this:

1. The navigation hierarchy
    - Icon and Server name _(for example Promptbook Agents Server)_
    - arrow ">" and Agents or picked agent name (organized in folders)
    - arrow ">" and the view Profile / Chat / Book of the agent or nothing if no agent is picked
2. The menu items
    - Documentation
    - System
3. Control panel and user menu
    - Control panel
    - User menu with the avatar and the name of the user

#### Database migrations for Agents server _(as additional context)_

-   Migrations are located in `apps/agents-server/src/database/migrations`
-   Be aware that table names in migrations have prefix `prefix_` _(look at existing migrations for reference)_
-   Migrations should be backwards compatible:
    -   Meaning that earlier versions of the server should be able to run with the database after migration without any issues.
    -   This is important because we want to have the same database for production and preview environments.
    -   This database will be migrated to the latest version of the preview environment, but the production environment should be able to run with it without any issues.
    -   The only thing that can happen is that older versions of the server will not be able to use new features.
    -   Adding new columns, tables, etc. is fine, but do not remove or rename existing ones, and do not change the meaning of existing columns or tables.
    -   When in doubt, prefer to add new things instead of changing existing ones.

#### Metadata of Agents server _(as additional context)_

-   There is a table called `Metadata`.
-   It has `key` and `value` fields.
-   It is a similar concept to configuration, but this configuration can be changed by administrators in the Agents Server website.

#### Book Language blueprint _(as additional context)_

Book language is a domain-specific language used for defining AI agents in the Promptbook Engine and Agents server.
It has lightweight syntax and keywords (the commitments) that allow you to define the "soul" of the agent.
The book language is designed to be human-readable and easy to write, while also being powerful enough to express complex agent behaviors.

Every agent has its source defined in the book language, which is called "agent source". The agent source is parsed and processed by the Promptbook Engine to create the actual AI agent that can interact with users and perform tasks.
This agent source is internally converted to a structured format called "agent model requirements" which are the actual raw technical instructions for the AI model to run the agent.

There is a standalone book language documentation on each agent server on `/api/docs/book.md` route, for example `https://live.ptbk.io/api/docs/book-language.md?language=en`.
Use it as a reference for the syntax and semantics of the book language, and modify `apps/agents-server/src/utils/bookLanguageDocumentation/createStandaloneBookLanguageMarkdown.ts` if it is relevant to the change you are doing.

##### Commitments _(as additional context and part of Book Language)_

Commitments are basic syntax elements that add specific functionalities to AI agents written in `book` language.

-   They are used in `agentSource`, there are commitments like `PERSONA`, `RULE`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE CALENDAR`, `USE PROJECT`, `META IMAGE`, `CLOSED`, etc.
-   They are in the folder `src/commitments`.
-   Each commitment starts with a keyword, e.g. `PERSONA`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE PROJECT`, etc. on a beginning of the line and ends by a new commitment or the end of the book.
-   There is a general pattern that the commitment keyword is followed by a space and then by the content of the commitment, for example:
    -   `PERSONA You are a helpful assistant that helps with cooking recipes.`
    -   `USE MCP https://mcp.example.com/server`
-   In the commitment context, you can reference external agents, for example:
    -   `TEAM You can talk to {Criminal lawyer} and {Financial advisor}`

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HaLodVoVXAKbJXtiayA4tN","type":"tool_result","content":"<system-reminder>This memory is 5 days old. Verify against current code before asserting as fact.</system-reminder>\n1\t---\n2\tname: ptbk-install-peer-warnings-task\n3\tdescription: \"\\\"[✨👉] When installing ptbk there are lot of peer dependency warnings\\\" — the zod 3 vs zod 4 split, why @promptbook/cli cannot just drop zod, and the fast --package-lock-only way to reproduce npm ERESOLVE\"\n4\tmetadata: \n5\t  node_type: memory\n6\t  type: project\n7\t  originSessionId: ae9faf42-babf-481b-a708-5164f847cb92\n8\t  modified: 2026-09-11T16:15:51.414Z\n9\t---\n10\t\n11\tFixed 2026-09-11. `npm i ptbk` printed 13 `ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` events; 10 of them were zod.\n12\t\n13\t**Root cause (two independent parts):**\n14\t1. The tree contained two irreconcilable zod families — `@ai-sdk/openai@1` / `@ai-sdk/google@1` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@0` peer-require `zod@^3.0.0` (every version of those majors does), while `@openai/agents` peer-requires `zod@^4.0.0` and the Agents Server itself imports zod 4. No single hoisted zod satisfies both. Fixed by upgrading to `@ai-sdk/openai@2.0.127` / `@ai-sdk/google@2.0.97` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@1.0.56` (peer `^3.25.76 || ^4.1.8`).\n15\t2. `bundleReferencesDependency` in `scripts/generate-packages/addDependenciesForGeneratedPackages.ts` substring-matched `from 'x'` anywhere in `packages/*/esm/index.es.js`, so the **code templates inside the transpilers** (`AgentOsTranspiler`, `AnthropicClaudeManagedTranspiler` emit `import { z } from 'zod';` for the *transpiled* project) made `@promptbook/core` publish `zod`, `dotenv` and `@anthropic-ai/sdk` as real dependencies. Fixed by requiring `import`/`export` needles to sit on a line that *starts* with the keyword (rollup always emits real imports at column 0); `require(`/`import(` calls still match anywhere.\n16\t\n17\t**Why:** these traps are invisible from the code — the `zod` pin looks deliberate, and the obvious \"just drop zod from `@promptbook/cli`\" is wrong.\n18\t\n19\t**How to apply:**\n20\t- **Do not** try to remove `zod` (or any root dependency) from `@promptbook/cli`: `rollup.config.js` gives the cli `additionalDependencies: [..., ...Object.keys(dependencies)]`, i.e. *all* root deps, because the cli ships `apps/agents-server` and that app imports zod (`managementApiSchemas.ts`, MCP route). The cli must keep it.\n21\t- **Do not** jump to the newest `@ai-sdk/*`: `@ai-sdk/openai@4` / `google@4` / `deepseek@3` (and `@ai-sdk/provider-utils@5`) declare `engines: node >=22`, which would break the repo's `engines: node >=18.18.0`. The `2.x`/`1.x` line accepts zod 4 and still says `node >=18`.\n22\t- Upgrading past `@ai-sdk/*@1` forces a `LanguageModelV1 → V2` migration of `src/llm-providers/vercel/createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider.ts` (used by Google **and** Deepseek): `provider.chat(modelId)` takes no settings, `doGenerate` loses `inputFormat`/`mode`, the result is `content: Array<{type,...}>` instead of `text`, and usage is `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`. `npm run test-types` verifies all of it because the request is typed `Parameters<typeof model.doGenerate>[0]`.\n23\t- **Reproduce/verify npm warnings in ~1 min instead of ~8:** `npm install ptbk@<version> --package-lock-only --no-audit --no-fund` in a scratch dir — registry metadata only, no tarballs, identical ERESOLVE output. To test a *candidate* manifest, write the generated `packages/cli/package.json` `dependencies` into a local `file:` package and resolve that.\n24\t- Compute the exact conflict list from the lockfile: walk `packages[*].peerDependencies`, resolve each peer by climbing `node_modules` segments, `semver.satisfies(..., {loose: true})` — **`loose` matters**, `@tailwindcss/typography` has an invalid range (`>=3.0.0 || insiders || ...`) that is a false positive without it.\n25\t- 3 warnings are unfixable from here: `swagger-ui-react`'s nested `react-copy-to-clipboard` / `react-debounce-input` / `react-inspector` cap React at 18 and are unmaintained. `swagger-ui-react` is really used (`apps/agents-server/src/app/swagger/SwaggerPageClient.tsx`).\n26\t- `@promptbook/cli` also exposed a separate defect worth knowing: `createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider` calls `model.doGenerate(rawRequest)` **twice** per prompt (double cost, half-counted usage) — reported in `agents-messages/2026-09-1100-vercel-adapter-calls-the-model-twice.message.md`, deliberately not fixed.\n27\t\n28\tRelated: [[ptbk-browser-bundle-jsdom-task]] (same generator, `browser` field), [[promptbook-verification-step-order]]\n29\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8f44f218-fe4b-4504-acd8-438e13a0f15f","uuid":"cee50ed5-e4f4-4305-90a1-a85ad4f8f75c","timestamp":"2026-09-17T12:34:56.344Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\.claude\\projects\\C--Users-me-work-ai-promptbook\\memory\\ptbk-install-peer-warnings-task.md","content":"---\nname:
