The current and latest commit cards, plus every pending-commit row, now visibly show the commit subject, full hash, and authored date.\n    -   Factored the time-behind suffix out of `buildDeploymentDriftLabel` into a new shared `buildDeploymentTimeBehindLabel` helper so the same localized `N days behind` text powers both the current-deployment card and the pending-commits card without duplication.\n    -   Added a new `GET /api/admin/update/log` route that streams the full persisted `self-update.log` file (gated by `isUserGlobalAdmin`) together with a `Content-Disposition` filename, backed by a new `readVpsSelfUpdateLogFileContent` helper in `vpsSelfUpdate.ts`.\n    -   When the latest update job's status is `failed`, the Update job card now shows **Copy log** and **Download log** buttons that hit the new endpoint and reuse the shared `downloadBlob` / `parseFilenameFromContentDisposition` helpers (same flow as the existing Backup export), so the admin can quickly share the full installer log with the developers for debugging instead of only seeing the truncated terminal tail.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server `/admin/update` self-update failing on the standalone VPS during the post-compile `Linting and checking validity of types ...` phase with `next-build exited with code null.` (the Node build process was being killed by the OS, typically by the OOM killer, after webpack had already retried minification multiple times). The shared `other/vps/install.sh` `build_agents_server` step now sets `PTBK_AGENTS_SERVER_IGNORE_NEXT_VALIDATION=true` so the VPS production build skips the duplicate Next.js lint + TypeScript validation step that is already enforced by repository CI, matching the existing CLI materialized-runtime build path and letting the self-update finish reliably on memory-constrained VPS hosts.\n\n-   Changed the Agents Server durable chat progress card so each preparation phase shows the **real runtime state** that has actually been resolved so far, instead of a fixed scripted blurb that was identical for every chat turn:\n\n    -   `createUserChatProgressCard` now accepts a `UserChatProgressContext` object and composes the `now`/`next` markdown from real signals — resolved agent name, attachment count, configured tool count and friendly tool labels (e.g. `web browser`, `web search`, `email sending`), knowledge-source count, calendar/email/project integrations, the resolved LLM provider title, and whether the AgentKit runtime came from the in-process cache.\n    -   `createRunUserChatJobExecutionContext` builds that context incrementally as the worker resolves new information and forwards it through `reportProgress` at every phase, so the user sees, for example, **\"Loading the instructions and configured commitments for agent Cooking Coach (2 knowledge sources)\"** instead of the previous static **\"Preparing the agent instructions and context needed for this request.\"**\n    -   The `starting_response` update is now emitted **after** the AgentKit cache lookup completes, so the progress text can name the actual provider (e.g. **\"Calling the language model via OpenAI\"**) and call out whether the agent had to be prepared fresh.\n    -   Added a small `resolveUserChatProgressToolHighlights` helper that maps technical commitment tool identifiers (`web_search`, `useBrowser`, `send_email`, …) to short user-facing labels and excludes the internal `agent_progress` / `assistant_preparation` tools that should never appear as user-relevant capabilities.\n    -   Updated the queued-message lifecycle copy to reflect the actual queueing state (**\"Your message is waiting in the queue for the next available worker to pick it up.\"**) and updated `userChatMessageLifecycle.test.ts` accordingly.\n\n-   Added a new `Octopus 3D 4` built-in avatar visual as a smoother, blobbier continuation of `Octopus 3D 3`, and promoted it to the new shared `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL`:\n\n    -   Reused the seeded `Octopus3` morphology profile together with the shared projected-eye and projected-mouth helpers so the new proper-3D octopus stays consistent with the rest of the octopus family without duplicating face-rendering logic.\n    -   Rendered the whole octopus as one continuous blobby mesh sampled at a higher latitude/longitude resolution so the silhouette reads as a round, real-octopus body with eight tentacle lobes that smoothly fuse into the mantle instead of attaching as separate ribbons.\n    -   Drove the tentacle motion with a combined primary, secondary, and slow-curl sine harmonic per lobe so the tentacles wave naturally and continuously, like a real octopus drifting in water, while remaining cute and simple.\n    -   Added a richer multi-pass shading pipeline (key light, rim light, soft gloss highlight, seeded pigment spots, and per-patch outline) on top of the existing palette tones, so the silhouette feels textured and visually appealing without leaving the simple flat-stylized look.\n    -   Kept avatar pointer tracking on both the full mesh silhouette and the projected eyes — the head turns toward the mouse cursor more responsively than `Octopus 3D 3` and the eyes track the pointer inside the rotated head.\n    -   Switched the shared `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL_ID` to `octopus3d4`, updated the Agents Server `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL` metadata default + allowed-values note to include `OCTOPUS3D4`, and added a backwards-compatible database migration that upgrades existing `OCTOPUS3D3` defaults to `OCTOPUS3D4` while preserving any administrator-customized value.\n\n-   Fixed broken access control on chat history, chat feedback, and agent CRUD routes of Agents Server. Multiple route handlers guarded themselves with `getCurrentUser()` (i.e. \"the caller is logged in\") but never checked that the **specific record** being read, modified, or deleted belonged to the caller or that the caller was an administrator, so any authenticated user — including self-registered unprivileged users — could read, mutate, or destroy data that belonged to other users / other agents:\n\n    -   `/api/chat-history` (`GET`/`DELETE`), `/api/chat-history/[id]` (`DELETE`), `/api/chat-history/export` (`GET`), `/api/chat-feedback` (`GET`/`DELETE`), and `/api/chat-feedback/export` (`GET`) returned (or deleted) the **entire** `ChatHistory` / `ChatFeedback` tables across every agent and user. These endpoints power the admin-only `/admin/chat-history` and `/admin/chat-feedback` screens — which expose IPs, anonymous `userNote`s, and `expectedAnswer`s across all agents — so they are now gated by `isUserAdmin()` instead of `getCurrentUser()`, returning `401 Unauthorized` for non-administrators. The two admin pages and the agent-context-menu entries that link to them were updated to require admin as well, so non-administrators no longer see dead-end links to those screens.\n    -   `PATCH /api/agents/[agentName]` (rename / change visibility) and `DELETE /api/agents/[agentName]` (tombstone) never resolved the agent's owner. Both handlers now resolve the target agent through a new shared `findAgentForCallerWriteAccess` helper that combines `findOwnedAgentByIdentifier` (reusing the same ownership primitive as the v1 management API) with an `isUserAdmin()` admin override, and reject with `404 Not Found` when the agent does not belong to the caller and the caller is not an administrator. The visibility update is now scoped to the resolved row by primary key instead of matching every agent that shares the supplied name or permanent id. The new helper also covers legacy `ADMIN_PASSWORD` administrators that have no database user id.\n\n-   Fixed SSRF vulnerability in three additional Agents Server endpoints that accepted a caller-supplied URL and fetched it server-side without authentication and without the existing `assertSafeUrl` SSRF guard:\n\n    -   `/api/page-preview/screenshot` opened the URL in a headless Playwright browser (which executes JavaScript on the fetched page) and returned a PNG screenshot. The only validation was that the scheme was `http:` or `https:`, so an unauthenticated attacker could screenshot `http://127.0.0.1`, `http://169.254.169.254` (AWS / GCP / Azure metadata service), or any RFC-1918 private address.\n    -   `/api/page-preview/check` performed a server-side `fetch` (HEAD with `redirect: follow`) through `checkIfUrlCanBeEmbedded` with the same lack of validation.\n    -   `/api/team-agent-profile` called `fetchAgentProfile` against any URL that passed the structural `isValidAgentUrl` check and forwarded the internal team access token to the target. The same-origin check inside `createTeamInternalAgentAccessHeaders` already prevented the token from leaking to truly cross-origin URLs, but the SSRF itself was unblocked.\n\n    All three endpoints now require authentication (`getCurrentUser` returns `401 Unauthorized` for anonymous requests) and validate the destination URL through `assertSafeUrl` (the same helper that already protects `/api/scrape`) before any outbound `fetch` / `page.goto`, returning `400 Bad Request` for non-HTTP(S) schemes and private/internal IP destinations (loopback, RFC 1918, link-local / cloud-metadata, shared address space, IPv6 ULA / link-local / loopback). The chat citation iframe-fallback feature is unaffected because it runs inside the authenticated chat UI and previews public citation URLs. The `[👣][🧠]` TODO in `isValidAgentUrl` is resolved by keeping that function a pure structural validator and documenting that callers reaching untrusted networks must apply `assertSafeUrl` themselves.\n\n-   Fixed unauthenticated abuse of server-side paid AI APIs in Agents Server. Five route handlers proxied directly to paid third-party providers (OpenAI, ElevenLabs) using the **server's API keys** without any authentication check, so any anonymous client could drain the configured API credit and exhaust quotas by repeatedly calling them. All five routes are now protected by a new shared `guardPaidApiRequest` utility that combines authentication and per-identity sliding-window rate limiting (DRY for all paid-proxy endpoints):\n\n    -   `/api/chat` and `/api/chat-streaming` were OpenAI smoke-test endpoints with no frontend usage. They are now gated behind `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` and return `404` in production so they cannot be exploited even if the deployment exposes them.\n    -   `/api/openai/v1/audio/transcriptions` now requires authentication (signed session cookie or `Authorization: Bearer ptbk_…` API key), enforces a 25 MB upload size limit, validates the `model` parameter against an allowlist of supported OpenAI transcription models (`gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, `whisper-1`), validates `language` against ISO-639-1, and truncates the optional transcription `prompt` to 800 characters.\n    -   `/api/elevenlabs/tts` now requires authentication and validates the caller-supplied `voiceId` against the strict ElevenLabs format (15–40 alphanumeric characters), preventing path-segment injection into the upstream URL and rejecting unknown voices that would still bill the ElevenLabs account.\n    -   `/api/images/[filename]` now requires authentication and validates `modelName`, `size`, `quality`, and `style` query parameters against fixed allowlists (DALL·E / Gemini image models, supported sizes, `standard`/`hd`, `vivid`/`natural`) before forwarding to the paid image generation provider.\n    -   The shared guard applies a per-identity sliding-window rate limit on top of authentication — by username for cookie sessions, by hashed API key for bearer auth, and by request IP for any anonymous fallback. Budgets are tier-specific (60/min for transcription and TTS, 20/min for image generation), so a single compromised account cannot sustain large bills. Rejected requests receive `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header.\n\n-   Fixed authentication bypass in Agents Server `validateApiKey`: the helper previously treated the presence of any `sessionToken` cookie as proof of a valid browser session, so any client could forge `Cookie: sessionToken=anything` and gain unauthenticated access to every endpoint behind `validateApiKey` (including the OpenAI-compatible chat-completion routes that consume server-side API credits). The helper now parses the cookie value with the existing `parseSessionToken` HMAC-signature verifier and only accepts the request when the signature matches, restoring the original intent of the browser-session shortcut without trusting attacker-supplied cookies.\n\n-   Optimized Agents Server directory and chat-sidebar reads for standalone VPS and Supabase deployments:\n\n    -   Added SQLite read indexes for active agent/folder directory scans, chat sidebar lists, and active chat job/timeout polling used by the homepage, agent navigation, and chat pages.\n    -   Added matching PostgreSQL indexes for active agent/folder directory reads and creation-time chat sidebar ordering.\n    -   Invalidated cached active organization snapshots after agent source, visibility, create, delete, and restore mutations so optimized homepage/menu data refreshes immediately.\n\n-   Fixed timing attack vulnerability in Agents Server admin password verification: all three comparison sites (`isUserGlobalAdmin`, `getCurrentUser`, `authenticateUser`) now use a shared `isAdminPasswordEqual` utility that calls Node.js's `timingSafeEqual` (from the `crypto` module) instead of JavaScript's `===` operator, preventing character-by-character password inference via response-time measurement.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server durable chat progress so new agent responses show structured real progress from the queued and preparation phases instead of a synthetic immediate pre-answer:\n\n    -   Queued assistant placeholders now render a progress card with current step, next step, and checklist state.\n    -   The durable chat worker updates that card while it reads context, prepares the agent, checks available tools/inputs, and starts the response.\n    -   The `agent_progress` tool instructions now ask the real agent to report concise user-facing decisions, actions, and results without exposing hidden chain-of-thought or raw technical details.\n\n-   Fixed SSRF vulnerability in the Agents Server `/api/scrape` endpoint:\n\n    -   The endpoint now requires authentication — unauthenticated requests receive a `401 Unauthorized` response.\n    -   Added URL validation via a new `assertSafeUrl` utility that rejects non-HTTP(S) schemes and destination hostnames that resolve to private/internal IP ranges (RFC 1918: `10.x`, `172.16–31.x`, `192.168.x`; loopback `127.x`; link-local / cloud-metadata `169.254.x`; shared address space `100.64.x`; IPv6 ULA, link-local, and loopback). Blocked requests receive a `400 Bad Request` response.\n\n-   Fixed package publishing for `@promptbook/cli` by marking the `ptbk coder server` HTTP/UI helpers as CLI-only instead of never-publishable, matching the existing CLI command import chain.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder find-unwritten` command that lists all prompt sections whose body still contains the `@@@` authoring placeholder:\n\n    -   Prints a summary line (done / for agent / to be written counts) followed by a numbered list of unwritten prompts with their file path, line number, and first summary line.\n    -   Accepts `--priority <n>` to apply the same minimum-priority filter used by `ptbk coder run`.\n    -   Reuses the existing `listPromptsToBeWritten` / `printPromptsToBeWritten` utilities so the detection logic stays in one place.\n\n-   Added `--agent <agent-book-path>` option to `ptbk coder run` and `ptbk coder server`:\n\n    -   Accepts a path to a `.book` file (relative to the current working directory) whose compiled system message is prepended to each coding prompt before the task text.\n    -   Can be combined with `--context`: the agent system message is inserted first, followed by the task prompt, and finally the context — so the harness sees agent instructions → task → additional context.\n    -   Example: `ptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh --context AGENTS.md --agent agents/coding-expert.book`\n\n-   `ptbk coder init` now automatically generates 5 prompt boilerplate files after setting up the project configuration.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder server` command that runs the same prompt-processing logic as `ptbk coder run` but keeps the process alive and serves a kanban web UI on a configurable port (default `4441`):\n\n    -   The server polls for new prompt files every 5 seconds instead of exiting when all prompts are done or none are ready, making it suitable as a long-running background service.\n    -   A kanban board at `http://localhost:4441` shows all prompt sections grouped into four columns: **To Do**, **Not Ready**, **Done**, and **Failed**.\n    -   Each card is clickable and opens a Trello-style edit modal where the prompt text can be modified and saved back to the source file immediately.\n    -   A **Play / Pause** button in the browser header is kept in sync with the CLI pause state; clicking it calls the same `requestPause` / `requestResume` functions used by the `p` key in the terminal.\n    -   The HTTP server exposes a small REST API: `GET /api/prompts`, `GET /api/status`, `POST /api/pause`, `POST /api/resume`, and `PUT /api/prompts/update`.\n    -   All options from `ptbk coder run` are supported (`--harness`, `--model`, `--thinking-level`, `--context`, `--test`, `--wait`, `--priority`, `--no-commit`, etc.) plus a new `--port` option (or `PTBK_CODER_SERVER_PORT` env var).\n    -   The frontend source lives in `apps/coder-server/index.html` and is served inline by the Node.js HTTP server (no build step required).\n\n-   Added a VSCode extension (`apps/vscode-extension`) for the Book language that provides syntax highlighting for `.book` and `.ptbk` files. The TextMate grammar (`syntaxes/book.tmLanguage.json`) is dynamically generated from `COMMITMENT_REGISTRY` by running `npm run generate-vscode-grammar`, ensuring the extension always reflects the current set of commitment keywords. Publishing to the Visual Studio Code Marketplace is available through `npm run build:vscode-extension -- --publish`, which generates the grammar, syncs a Marketplace-safe extension version from the root `package.json`, publishes with `vsce`, and creates the VSIX artifact.\n\n-   Fixed `<BookEditor/>` syntax highlighting incorrectly highlighting the local part of email addresses (e.g. `team@foo.bar`) as agent references. `@`-style references now require whitespace or start-of-line before the `@` sign, so only `@Paul` (with preceding whitespace) is highlighted, not `team@foo.bar`. Removed a now-redundant manual preceding-character check that duplicated this logic.\n\n-   Improved `<BookEditor/>` syntax highlighting to dynamically detect commitments — any line starting with one or more all-uppercase words (minimum 2 characters each) is now highlighted as a commitment keyword, without relying on a hardcoded list of known commitment types. Lines starting with a dash or a single uppercase letter are not affected. Special commitment types (`NOTE`, `NOTES`, `NONCE`, `TODO`) retain their distinct colors, and `FROM`/`IMPORT`/`IMPORTS`/`TEAM` retain agent-reference link highlighting.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server VPS installation failing on the first run with a Node.js out-of-memory crash during the Next.js production build. The `ptbk agents-server build` command now passes `--max-old-space-size=4096` in `NODE_OPTIONS` when spawning the webpack compilation process, allowing the ~1.9 GiB peak heap usage to succeed within the swap-backed memory budget enforced by the installer. Existing `NODE_OPTIONS` values are preserved; the flag is only injected when no `--max-old-space-size` is already set.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server file upload URLs for self-contained S3 to hide the internal bucket name, path prefix, and directory structure. Files are now stored under a content-addressed key (`{hash[0]}/{hash[1]}/{sha256}/{filename}`) and served through a new Next.js proxy route (`/s3/{hex}/{hex}/{hash}/{filename}`) so the public URL is unguessable and reveals no internal storage details. Old-style URLs (e.g. `/s3/promptbook-files/ptbk-agents/user/files/…`) remain accessible for backwards compatibility.\n\n-   Fixed citation source previews in Agents Server chat failing silently when the target page blocks iframe embedding via `X-Frame-Options` (e.g. `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`). The chat modal now checks embeddability server-side before rendering and falls back to a server-taken screenshot with an \"Open in new tab\" link when the page cannot be framed.\n\n-   Optimized Agents Server database layer to prevent the server from becoming unresponsive under load:\n\n    -   Added `connectionTimeoutMillis` (15 s) to the shared PostgreSQL connection pool so queries fail fast when all connections are busy instead of queuing indefinitely — the root cause of the server becoming completely unresponsive after a period of high traffic.\n    -   Increased the default pool size from 10 to 20 connections (configurable via `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` environment variable) to handle more concurrent chat-stream polling and atomic-SQL operations without exhausting the pool.\n    -   Added `idleTimeoutMillis` (30 s) and `allowExitOnIdle` so unused connections are closed promptly, keeping memory and socket usage low.\n    -   Added a pool `error` event handler so unexpected errors on idle clients are logged instead of propagating as unhandled exceptions that can corrupt the pool state.\n    -   Added a 30-second hard timeout to every Supabase HTTP request via a custom `fetch` wrapper on the server-side Supabase client. Without this, a slow or temporarily unreachable PostgREST endpoint would cause Supabase queries to hang indefinitely, holding Node.js event-loop resources and contributing to the gradual unresponsiveness over time.\n\n-   Added `isVerbose` option to `CliAgent` so callers can enable the same harness-level console output that `ptbk agent exec --verbose` produces without spawning the CLI. `LiteAgent` already supported `isVerbose`; both classes now expose the option consistently.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat runner not including the agent's initial message (defined via `INITIAL MESSAGE` commitment) in the queued book file when a user sends their first message. The local and external chat runners now prepend the agent's initial message as the opening `MESSAGE @Agent` block so the agent runner sees the full conversation context from the start.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat messages being silently cropped when the agent response contained a line starting with a single uppercase ASCII letter followed by lowercase text (e.g. \"V části...\" in Czech). `Book.parse` was incorrectly treating such lines as commitment headers due to an overly permissive regex in `parseCommitmentHeader`. The fix tightens the regex to require at least two characters in the first keyword word, which prevents common natural-language words like \"V\" (Czech for \"in\") or \"A\" / \"I\" in English from being mistaken for commitment markers.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server chat tray ordering from last-activity time to creation time so chats stay in their chronological position and browsing an older chat no longer moves it to the top of the list.\n\n-   Optimized animated avatar rendering performance in Agents Server to fix 1–2 fps drops when multiple avatars are visible:\n\n    -   Throttled the shared animation loop to ~24 fps (from the display refresh rate of 60 fps+) via a frame-interval gate in `avatarAnimationScheduler.ts`. Animated octopus visuals change slowly enough that 24 fps is perceptually identical to 60 fps while reducing total render work by ~60%.\n    -   Cached stable per-avatar data (morphology profile, animation phase, tentacle profiles, eye phase offsets) using a `WeakMap` keyed on the `createRandom` factory reference in `octopus3dAvatarVisual`, `octopus3d2AvatarVisual`, and `octopus3d3AvatarVisual`. These values are deterministic given the avatar definition and were previously recomputed on every frame.\n    -   Replaced `context.filter = 'blur()'` shadow effects in all six affected visuals (`octopus3d`, `octopus3d2`, `octopus3d3`, `minecraft`, `minecraft2`, `fractal`) with equivalent gradient-based approximations. CSS filter blur forces the browser into a full software rasterization pass on every frame; the gradient alternative is hardware-accelerated and visually equivalent.\n    -   Added `\"ts-node\": { \"transpileOnly\": true }` to `tsconfig.json` so the CLI integration test (`ts-node src/cli/test/ptbk.ts --help`) skips full type-checking during execution. Type correctness is still enforced by the dedicated `test-types` step; this change brings the CLI startup from an uncapped compile pass (> 5 min on Windows) down to ~20 seconds.\n\n-   Further optimized animated avatar rendering performance in Agents Server, building on the earlier 24 fps throttle and stable-state cache. With twelve animated octopus avatars on a single page the previous pass still left the UI at 1–2 fps because every visible avatar fired on the same animation frame and the per-frame mesh sampling cost remained heavy:\n\n    -   Interleaved listeners in `avatarAnimationScheduler.ts` so animated avatars no longer all render on the same animation frame. Each listener now tracks its own last-run timestamp, new listeners are phase-staggered at registration, and the shared loop runs at most `MAX_AVATAR_LISTENERS_PER_FRAME` (= 2) listeners per `requestAnimationFrame`, scheduling the rest on subsequent frames. Each avatar still reaches the 24 fps target individually; total per-frame work is bounded regardless of how many avatars are visible.\n    -   Added per-frame corner-grid sample caching to `octopus3d3AvatarVisual` and `octopus3d2AvatarVisual`. The mesh patch loop previously called `sampleContinuousOctopusSurfacePoint` / `sampleBlobbyOctopusSurfacePoint` for each of the four corners of every patch (16×40×4 = 2 560 samples per frame for `octopus3d3`), even though most corners are shared between neighboring patches. The new implementation precomputes a `(latitudePatchCount + 1) × (longitudePatchCount + 1)` corner grid once per frame, cutting the sample call count by ~3.7× on `octopus3d3` and ~4× on `octopus3d2`.\n    -   Added per-frame longitude caching for `resolveContinuousTentacleInfluence`, `resolveContinuousLobeWave`, and `resolveLowerLobeWave` in the same two visuals. Each tentacle-influence evaluation runs an 8-iteration `Math.exp` loop over the seeded tentacle profiles, so calling it once per longitude grid value instead of once per corner cuts the dominant inner-loop cost by ~30×. The new `sampleContinuousOctopusSurfacePointWithLongitudeCache` / `sampleBlobbyOctopusSurfacePointWithLongitudeCache` helpers accept the cached values explicitly; the existing public sample functions are preserved for off-grid callers (eyes, mouth).\n\n-   Added `--wait [duration]` flag to `ptbk coder run` for controlling the delay between prompt rounds:\n\n    -   `--wait 1h` (or `--wait 30m`, `--wait 5s`, combinations like `--wait 1h30m`) waits the specified duration between rounds to avoid hitting harness rate limits. The first prompt executes immediately; the wait is inserted only before subsequent rounds.\n    -   `--wait` without a value retains the existing interactive behavior — waits for user confirmation before each prompt.\n    -   No flag (or `--no-wait`) means no waiting, which is now the default. `--no-wait` is kept for backward compatibility.\n\n-   Fixed `CliAgent` failing with `Missing --harness in non-dry run mode` when no `harness` is provided: `CliAgent` now falls back to the `PTBK_HARNESS` environment variable, mirroring `ptbk agent exec` behavior. Similarly falls back to `PTBK_MODEL` and `PTBK_THINKING_LEVEL` env vars. Extracted shared env-var constants (`PTBK_HARNESS_ENV`, `PTBK_MODEL_ENV`, `PTBK_THINKING_LEVEL_ENV`), harness names (`CLI_AGENT_HARNESS_NAMES`), and thinking-level values (`CLI_AGENT_THINKING_LEVEL_VALUES`) into the new `src/book-3.0/cliAgentEnv.ts` so CLI and library share a single source of truth. readability and maintainability.\n-   Fix width of the message in the chat by adding a minimum width and improving layout for short messages.\n-   Use model `gemini-3-pro-image-preview` for the agent of Avatar Images\n-   Updated `openai` from `4.63.0` to `6.18.0` and fixed all resulting type errors.\n-   Resolved `zod` peer dependency conflicts between `@ai-sdk/deepseek` and `@openai/agents` by using `overrides` in `package.json`.\n-   Fixed `node-fetch` declaration issue in `LindatAutomaticTranslator.ts` by using native `URLSearchParams` and removing `node-fetch` import.\n-   Stabilized Agents Server under low traffic by removing constant 5-second DB polling from timeout/preparation workers, restoring durable timeout wake-ups through Vercel cron, fixing agent-source cycle detection across canonical/name URLs, and reducing agent-reference resolver churn.\n-   Logged richer durable diagnostics for failed Agents Server chat turns so admin task inspection no longer stops at the generic lease-expired summary:\n\n    -   Added backwards-compatible `failureDetails` storage for `UserChatJob` rows and now persist structured JSON diagnostics containing the failure summary, serialized error payload (message/name/stack when available), provider, timing, and chat-turn identifiers.\n    -   Reused the same diagnostics builder for runtime failures, unexpected worker-route failures, and expired-lease recovery paths to keep failure logging DRY and consistent.\n    -   Extended the admin task manager to surface the stored diagnostics under failed chat-completion tasks via an expandable \"Show details\" panel in the Last error column.\n\n-   Refactored Agents Server `apps/agents-server/src/app/agents/[agentName]/api/chat/route.ts` into smaller focused private chat-route helpers without changing external behavior:\n\n    -   Moved request-time runtime assembly, disclaimer and credential resolution, history initialization, and frozen team-member chat persistence behind the private `resolveAgentChatRouteContext` and `createTeamMemberFrozenChatPersistence` facades so `route.ts` now reads as a thin HTTP entrypoint.\n    -   Extracted the long-lived markdown stream orchestration, cancellation handling, tool-call framing, and final post-processing into the private `createAgentChatStreamResponse` helper while preserving the existing stateless chat streaming behavior, keep-alives, history recording, learning, and calendar activity logging.\n\n-   Enhanced the Agents Server new-agent wizard team step so it now behaves as a homepage-style multi-select picker:\n\n    -   Removed the separate manual \"Team members\" entry UI and kept only the existing-agents picker headed by \"Browse existing agents\" / \"Vyberte existující agenty\".\n    -   Kept multi-selection for teammate agents across the local server and federated servers while continuing to exclude the hidden core server from federated lists.\n    -   Extracted a shared homepage-like `AgentCardsSection` renderer so the wizard and federated-agent surfaces reuse the same card-grid, loading, empty, and error presentation.\n\n-   Improved Agents Server expired chat-worker diagnostics so the stale \"Background worker lease expired before the chat turn finished.\" failure now leaves actionable evidence instead of a generic summary:\n\n    -   Added shared expired-lease diagnostics for durable chat jobs that record queue/run/heartbeat timing, worker runtime thresholds, configured server limits, and a snapshot of active chat jobs and timeouts at the moment recovery runs.\n    -   Started logging structured `lease_expired` recovery/reconciliation events so server logs show which background tasks were active and whether the job had already outlived the 300-second worker route limit when heartbeats stopped.\n\n-   Added immediate optimistic profile-to-chat navigation in Agents Server, so starting a first message from an agent profile now swaps to the chat route without waiting for the server and keeps the user bubble visible throughout the handoff:\n\n    -   Persisted profile-to-chat optimistic turn metadata across the route transition, including the client message id reused later for canonical reconciliation and failure states.\n    -   Added a chat-route loading surface that renders the pending user turn right away while the standalone chat page server data is still loading.\n    -   Tightened optimistic/canonical merge ordering so unresolved user bubbles stay ahead of later assistant streaming messages until the server confirms them.\n\n-   Added the new deterministic `AsciiOctopus` avatar visual alongside the existing avatar set, with an animated ASCII-art rendering that keeps the same organic alien octopus feel as `Octopus3` while varying its blob silhouette, tentacle count, face, and colors from the agent name, hash, colors, and animation time:\n\n    -   Added the new built-in `ascii-octopus` canvas renderer to the shared avatar registry without changing the existing `Octopus`, `Octopus2`, `Octopus3`, pixel-art, Minecraft, or Fractal visuals.\n    -   Kept the implementation DRY by reusing shared octopus body and tentacle geometry helpers, while translating that geometry into deterministic ASCII glyphs instead of painted surfaces.\n    -   Updated the existing utils `/avatars` playground and regression coverage so the new renderer appears in the selector, preview grid, deterministic sample gallery, and supported URL-state parsing without creating a separate page.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server metadata enum handling so predefined metadata keys no longer accept arbitrary strings in `/admin/metadata`:\n\n    -   Added shared metadata definitions with reusable predefined option lists, so enum-like metadata such as `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL`, `SERVER_LANGUAGE`, `SERVER_VISIBILITY`, `CHAT_FEEDBACK_MODE`, `CHAT_VISUAL_MODE`, `NAME_POOL`, `DEFAULT_VISIBILITY`, and `NEW_AGENT_WIZARD` now render as selects instead of free-form text inputs.\n    -   Reused the same option registries across the metadata page and existing server-creation flows to keep enum values centralized and DRY.\n    -   Added server-side validation for predefined metadata options, so invalid enum values are rejected even when `/api/metadata` is called directly.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk agent-folder run` / `ptbk agent-folder tick` with the GitHub Copilot runner on Windows/MSYS for large queued-message prompts:\n\n    -   Stopped passing the full generated agent prompt as one `copilot -p \"...\"` shell argument, which could exceed the shell/Node argument-length limit and fail with `Argument list too long`.\n    -   Switched the GitHub Copilot runner to feed prompts through standard input instead, keeping `--model`, `--reasoning-effort`, and the existing non-interactive flags unchanged.\n    -   Added regression coverage for the new stdin-based invocation shape so agent-mode prompts stay safe even when the Book Language blueprint makes them much larger than coder prompts.\n\n-   Enhanced the `ptbk agent-folder run` rich terminal UI so it now reflects queued-message workflows instead of mirroring `ptbk coder run`:\n\n    -   The top branding now uses compact initials derived from the local `agent.book` title, making the dashboard identify the actual agent definition rather than only the runner selected by `--harness`.\n    -   The session summary now distinguishes the local agent from the execution runner and shows queue-specific totals (`finished` / `queued` / total) with a progress bar based on answered messages instead of `Task 1/1`.\n    -   Added a dedicated `User message` box that shows the latest `MESSAGE @User` block 1:1 with line-preserving trimming, while keeping the live streaming output panel unchanged.\n\n-   Enhanced the `ptbk agent-folder run` terminal dashboard so long-running agent sessions stay inside one stable rich UI:\n\n    -   Kept a single persistent boxed UI alive across queued-message runs, moving idle watching and idle auto-pull activity into explicit in-frame `WAITING` / loading states instead of printing plain lines that broke the layout mid-session.\n    -   Changed the header visual to render the local agent name in a smaller compact banner instead of large initials, while keeping the rest of the terminal frame layout intact.\n    -   Kept the queued-thread preview focused on the latest `MESSAGE @User` from the `.book` thread via `src/book-3.0/Book.ts`, and deferred the coding-agent Git identity tip until process exit so it no longer interrupts active sessions or `--no-ui` streaming output.\n\n-   Refactored `OpenAiAssistantExecutionTools` internals to keep OpenAI Assistants behavior unchanged while making the module easier to follow and maintain:\n\n    -   Split `src/llm-providers/openai/OpenAiAssistantExecutionTools.ts` into a smaller orchestration facade plus focused private helpers for prompt/thread building, tool-run execution, streaming/result reporting, and citation rewriting.\n    -   Kept assistant chat execution, tool progress streaming, hosted tool invocation, file attachment handling, assistant creation/update flows, and final Promptbook result export behavior unchanged while reducing the responsibility count inside the top-level file.\n\n-   Fixed the self-contained Stalwart mail server of Agents Server, which rejected every management call and therefore never routed inbound or outbound agent mail:\n\n    -   Fixed `install.sh`, which decided that Stalwart was already bootstrapped whenever `/etc/stalwart/config.json` existed. Stalwart writes that file itself - it is only its storage descriptor, for example `{\"@type\":\"RocksDb\",\"path\":\"/var/lib/stalwart/\",...}` - already during its very first startup, long before anything is bootstrapped, and never touches it again. The installer therefore skipped the `x:Bootstrap/set` call on **every** fresh installation and left the mail server permanently in bootstrap mode, where it refuses every management call with `{\"type\":\"forbidden\",\"description\":\"The server is in bootstrap mode. ...\"}`. The bootstrap state is now read from Stalwart itself through a management probe, so a pending bootstrap is completed on the next installer run and an already bootstrapped server is left untouched.\n    -   Fixed the Stalwart management payloads, which sent JSON arrays for `aliases`, `credentials`, `memberGroupIds`, `stages`, and the MTA hook `enable.match` expression, while Stalwart serializes every `set` / `objectList` property as an object and answered `invalidPatch` / `Invalid value for object property`. Added shared `toStalwartJmapSet` and `toStalwartJmapObjectList` helpers so all payloads build these shapes in one place.\n    -   Fixed `install.sh`, which provisioned the Agents Server Stalwart administrator inside the reserved `promptbook.invalid` domain. Stalwart rejects such a domain as an `Invalid domain name`, so the step failed and, because of `set -Eeuo pipefail`, aborted the whole installation before nginx, firewall, and certificate configuration ever ran. The bootstrap-time administrator credentials are now kept as Stalwart's fixed `STALWART_RECOVERY_ADMIN` credentials instead of provisioning a second administrator account.\n    -   Fixed the Stalwart step of `install.sh` aborting the whole installation when the mail server cannot be bootstrapped. Because `configure_firewall`, `configure_nginx_reverse_proxy`, and `configure_ssl_certificates` all run afterwards, a mail server problem used to leave the VPS without a firewall, reverse proxy, or certificates. The step now warns and continues, and the bootstrap is retried by every later installer run.\n    -   Fixed outbound submission, which was configured for port `587`, a port a bootstrapped Stalwart never opens. Agents Server now submits through `submissions` on port `465` with implicit TLS, and the email server administration pages document that port instead of `587`.\n    -   Fixed the catch-all address being assigned before the mailbox behind it existed, so synchronizing an already-known domain no longer fails on its first management call.\n    -   Improved Stalwart error reporting so a rejected object now includes Stalwart's own `notCreated` / `notUpdated` reason, and a server still in **bootstrap mode** reports an actionable message instead of a raw `forbidden` response.\n    -   Fixed the `promptbook-agents-server` build, which loaded the Next.js command line interface through the hardcoded path `../../node_modules/next/dist/bin/next`. That path does not exist inside a git worktree without its own installed dependencies, such as the `ptbk coder --isolate` worktrees, so `npm run build` failed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` even though Next.js was resolvable. The new `apps/agents-server/scripts/next-cli.js` resolves it through Node's own module resolution instead.\n\n-   Fixed the self-contained Stalwart mail server staying unusable whenever its initial setup was left pending. Completing that setup used to be the sole responsibility of `install.sh`, so a mail server which was installed before the bootstrap fix - or whose bootstrap failed once - answered every management call with `{\"type\":\"forbidden\",\"description\":\"The server is in bootstrap mode. ...\"}`, and **Synchronize Stalwart** on `/admin/email-server` could only report the error, never resolve it. Because the VPS self-update runs the _deployed_ release's installer, such a server stayed broken for at least one more update cycle. Agents Server now completes the bootstrap itself as the first step of every domain synchronization, which happens on startup and on **Synchronize Stalwart**, and it asks Stalwart for its bootstrap state instead of inferring it from files on disk. The setup Stalwart receives - mail hostname, default domain, automatic DKIM keys, and no ACME certificate request because nginx and certbot own every certificate on the VPS - is now defined by `buildStalwartBootstrapValue`, which `install.sh` mirrors under the shared `[📬]` marker because a fresh VPS is bootstrapped before Agents Server is built, and the result is verified against Stalwart itself so a bootstrap that was accepted but not applied is reported with the remaining manual step instead of a raw `forbidden` response. The installer keeps performing the bootstrap for a fresh installation and additionally waits until Stalwart really left bootstrap mode after the restart it needs to open its mail listeners, so the first synchronization of a newly started Agents Server no longer races a mail server that is still coming up.\n-   Improved the Agents Server **Book language manual** so its linked table of contents navigates directly to each commitment, and each end-to-end example links its used commitments back to their sections. The manual now describes `@Foo` and `{Foo foo}` as agent references rather than parameters, renames the `---` primitive to **Multiple agent**, documents code fences as ` ``` `, links every generated-from source to the Promptbook repository, hides parser/runtime implementation details and unfinished commitments, and keeps each commitment example focused on its canonical keyword with only `GOAL` and `CLOSED` as supporting syntax.\n\n-   Fixed the published `@promptbook/components` package, which broke the production build of every browser application that installs `ptbk`, `promptbook` or `@promptbook/components`. Rendered markdown is sanitized by `DOMPurify`, which needs a DOM, so `renderMarkdown` creates one through `jsdom` whenever it runs outside of a browser - for example during server-side rendering. That code path is unreachable in a browser, but bundlers resolve `require('jsdom')` statically, so `next build` followed it into `jsdom` and failed with **Module not found: Can't resolve `fs`** together with the same error for `child_process` and `net`. It failed even for an application that imports `<MarkdownContent/>` with `ssr: false`, because a bundler resolves a module it will never execute just as eagerly as one it will:\n\n    -   The generated manifest of every package that is not Node-only now declares `\"browser\": { \"jsdom\": false }`, which is the standard way to tell a browser bundler to replace a Node-only dependency with an empty module. Browser builds therefore no longer follow `jsdom` (and no longer ship it), while Node.js ignores the `browser` field and keeps resolving the real library for server-side rendering. The stubs are derived from the dependencies which the generated package really has, so a Node-only dependency which appears in a browser-facing package in the future is covered without another manual change.\n    -   Creating the server-side DOM moved from `renderMarkdown` into `$provideServerDomWindow`, which is now the single place where browser-facing code touches `jsdom`. A runtime that can provide neither the DOM of a browser nor `jsdom` is now reported as a branded `EnvironmentMismatchError` explaining why markdown can not be sanitized, instead of failing with `JSDOM is not a constructor`.\n    -   The list of Node-only packages is now shared through `isNodeOnlyPackage` between the publish-safety check and the dependency step of the package generation, instead of being written down twice.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":15,"oldLines":9,"newStart":15,"newLines":9,"lines":[" ","     The five remaining deprecation warnings cannot be resolved from this repository. `lodash.get` and","     `whatwg-encoding` are used by the newest `express-openapi-validator` and `jsdom` as well, `prebuild-install` is a","-    dependency of `better-sqlite3` which only its version 13 drops - and that version requires Node.js 22, while","-    Promptbook still supports Node.js 18 - and `crypto-js` and `@azure/openai` are deprecated by their authors but","-    really used by Promptbook.","+    dependency of `better-sqlite3` which only its version 13 drops - and that version requires Node.js 22, while the","+    `engines` of Promptbook still allow Node.js 18 - and `crypto-js` and `@azure/openai` are deprecated by their","+    authors but really used by Promptbook."," "," -   Reduced what `npm audit` reports after installing `ptbk` from 48 vulnerable packages to 15, and from 3 critical","     advisories to none. Every version pinned by Promptbook which an advisory named is raised to a release without that"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

Verify against current code before asserting as fact.</system-reminder>\n1\t---\n2\tname: ptbk-install-peer-warnings-task\n3\tdescription: \"\\\"[✨👉] When installing ptbk there are lot of peer dependency warnings\\\" — the zod 3 vs zod 4 split, why @promptbook/cli cannot just drop zod, and the fast --package-lock-only way to reproduce npm ERESOLVE\"\n4\tmetadata: \n5\t  node_type: memory\n6\t  type: project\n7\t  originSessionId: ae9faf42-babf-481b-a708-5164f847cb92\n8\t  modified: 2026-09-11T16:15:51.414Z\n9\t---\n10\t\n11\tFixed 2026-09-11. `npm i ptbk` printed 13 `ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` events; 10 of them were zod.\n12\t\n13\t**Root cause (two independent parts):**\n14\t1. The tree contained two irreconcilable zod families — `@ai-sdk/openai@1` / `@ai-sdk/google@1` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@0` peer-require `zod@^3.0.0` (every version of those majors does), while `@openai/agents` peer-requires `zod@^4.0.0` and the Agents Server itself imports zod 4. No single hoisted zod satisfies both. Fixed by upgrading to `@ai-sdk/openai@2.0.127` / `@ai-sdk/google@2.0.97` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@1.0.56` (peer `^3.25.76 || ^4.1.8`).\n15\t2. `bundleReferencesDependency` in `scripts/generate-packages/addDependenciesForGeneratedPackages.ts` substring-matched `from 'x'` anywhere in `packages/*/esm/index.es.js`, so the **code templates inside the transpilers** (`AgentOsTranspiler`, `AnthropicClaudeManagedTranspiler` emit `import { z } from 'zod';` for the *transpiled* project) made `@promptbook/core` publish `zod`, `dotenv` and `@anthropic-ai/sdk` as real dependencies. Fixed by requiring `import`/`export` needles to sit on a line that *starts* with the keyword (rollup always emits real imports at column 0); `require(`/`import(` calls still match anywhere.\n16\t\n17\t**Why:** these traps are invisible from the code — the `zod` pin looks deliberate, and the obvious \"just drop zod from `@promptbook/cli`\" is wrong.\n18\t\n19\t**How to apply:**\n20\t- **Do not** try to remove `zod` (or any root dependency) from `@promptbook/cli`: `rollup.config.js` gives the cli `additionalDependencies: [..., ...Object.keys(dependencies)]`, i.e. *all* root deps, because the cli ships `apps/agents-server` and that app imports zod (`managementApiSchemas.ts`, MCP route). The cli must keep it.\n21\t- **Do not** jump to the newest `@ai-sdk/*`: `@ai-sdk/openai@4` / `google@4` / `deepseek@3` (and `@ai-sdk/provider-utils@5`) declare `engines: node >=22`, which would break the repo's `engines: node >=18.18.0`. The `2.x`/`1.x` line accepts zod 4 and still says `node >=18`.\n22\t- Upgrading past `@ai-sdk/*@1` forces a `LanguageModelV1 → V2` migration of `src/llm-providers/vercel/createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider.ts` (used by Google **and** Deepseek): `provider.chat(modelId)` takes no settings, `doGenerate` loses `inputFormat`/`mode`, the result is `content: Array<{type,...}>` instead of `text`, and usage is `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`. `npm run test-types` verifies all of it because the request is typed `Parameters<typeof model.doGenerate>[0]`.\n23\t- **Reproduce/verify npm warnings in ~1 min instead of ~8:** `npm install ptbk@<version> --package-lock-only --no-audit --no-fund` in a scratch dir — registry metadata only, no tarballs, identical ERESOLVE output. To test a *candidate* manifest, write the generated `packages/cli/package.json` `dependencies` into a local `file:` package and resolve that.\n24\t- Compute the exact conflict list from the lockfile: walk `packages[*].peerDependencies`, resolve each peer by climbing `node_modules` segments, `semver.satisfies(..., {loose: true})` — **`loose` matters**, `@tailwindcss/typography` has an invalid range (`>=3.0.0 || insiders || ...`) that is a false positive without it.\n25\t- 3 warnings are unfixable from here: `swagger-ui-react`'s nested `react-copy-to-clipboard` / `react-debounce-input` / `react-inspector` cap React at 18 and are unmaintained. `swagger-ui-react` is really used (`apps/agents-server/src/app/swagger/SwaggerPageClient.tsx`).\n26\t- `@promptbook/cli` also exposed a separate defect worth knowing: `createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider` calls `model.doGenerate(rawRequest)` **twice** per prompt (double cost, half-counted usage) — reported in `agents-messages/2026-09-1100-vercel-adapter-calls-the-model-twice.message.md`, deliberately not fixed.\n27\t\n28\tRelated: [[ptbk-browser-bundle-jsdom-task]] (same generator, `browser` field), [[promptbook-verification-step-order]]\n29\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8f44f218-fe4b-4504-acd8-438e13a0f15f","uuid":"cee50ed5-e4f4-4305-90a1-a85ad4f8f75c","timestamp":"2026-09-17T12:34:56.344Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\.claude\\projects\\C--Users-me-work-ai-promptbook\\memory\\ptbk-install-peer-warnings-task.md","content":"---\nname: ptbk-install-peer-warnings-task\ndescription: \"\\\"[✨👉] When installing ptbk there are lot of peer dependency warnings\\\" — the zod 3 vs zod 4 split, why @promptbook/cli cannot just drop zod, and the fast --package-lock-only way to reproduce npm ERESOLVE\"\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: ae9faf42-babf-481b-a708-5164f847cb92\n  modified: 2026-09-11T16:15:51.414Z\n---\n\nFixed 2026-09-11. `npm i ptbk` printed 13 `ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` events; 10 of them were zod.\n\n**Root cause (two independent parts):**\n1. The tree contained two irreconcilable zod families — `@ai-sdk/openai@1` / `@ai-sdk/google@1` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@0` peer-require `zod@^3.0.0` (every version of those majors does), while `@openai/agents` peer-requires `zod@^4.0.0` and the Agents Server itself imports zod 4. No single hoisted zod satisfies both. Fixed by upgrading to `@ai-sdk/openai@2.0.127` / `@ai-sdk/google@2.0.97` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@1.0.56` (peer `^3.25.76 || ^4.1.8`).\n2. `bundleReferencesDependency` in `scripts/generate-packages/addDependenciesForGeneratedPackages.ts` substring-matched `from 'x'` anywhere in `packages/*/esm/index.es.js`, so the **code templates inside the transpilers** (`AgentOsTranspiler`, `AnthropicClaudeManagedTranspiler` emit `import { z } from 'zod';` for the *transpiled* project) made `@promptbook/core` publish `zod`, `dotenv` and `@anthropic-ai/sdk` as real dependencies. Fixed by requiring `import`/`export` needles to sit on a line that *starts* with the keyword (rollup always emits real imports at column 0); `require(`/`import(` calls still match anywhere.\n\n**Why:** these traps are invisible from the code — the `zod` pin looks deliberate, and the obvious \"just drop zod from `@promptbook/cli`\" is wrong.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- **Do not** try to remove `zod` (or any root dependency) from `@promptbook/cli`: `rollup.config.js` gives the cli `additionalDependencies: [..., ...Object.keys(dependencies)]`, i.e. *all* root deps, because the cli ships `apps/agents-server` and that app imports zod (`managementApiSchemas.ts`, MCP route). The cli must keep it.\n- **Do not** jump to the newest `@ai-sdk/*`: `@ai-sdk/openai@4` / `google@4` / `deepseek@3` (and `@ai-sdk/provider-utils@5`) declare `engines: node >=22`, which would break the repo's `engines: node >=18.18.0`. The `2.x`/`1.x` line accepts zod 4 and still says `node >=18`.\n- Upgrading past `@ai-sdk/*@1` forces a `LanguageModelV1 → V2` migration of `src/llm-providers/vercel/createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider.ts` (used by Google **and** Deepseek): `provider.chat(modelId)` takes no settings, `doGenerate` loses `inputFormat`/`mode`, the result is `content: Array<{type,...}>` instead of `text`, and usage is `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`. `npm run test-types` verifies all of it because the request is typed `Parameters<typeof model.doGenerate>[0]`.\n- **Reproduce/verify npm warnings in ~1 min instead of ~8:** `npm install ptbk@<version> --package-lock-only --no-audit --no-fund` in a scratch dir — registry metadata only, no tarballs, identical ERESOLVE output. To test a *candidate* manifest, write the generated `packages/cli/package.json` `dependencies` into a local `file:` package and resolve that.\n- Compute the exact conflict list from the lockfile: walk `packages[*].peerDependencies`, resolve each peer by climbing `node_modules` segments, `semver.satisfies(..., {loose: true})` — **`loose` matters**, `@tailwindcss/typography` has an invalid range (`>=3.0.0 || insiders || ...`) that is a false positive without it.\n- 3 warnings are unfixable from here: `swagger-ui-react`'s nested `react-copy-to-clipboard` / `react-debounce-input` / `react-inspector` cap React at 18 and are unmaintained. `swagger-ui-react` is really used (`apps/agents-server/src/app/swagger/SwaggerPageClient.tsx`).\n- `@promptbook/cli` also exposed a separate defect worth knowing: `createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider` calls `model.doGenerate(rawRequest)` **twice** per prompt (double cost, half-counted usage) — reported in `agents-messages/2026-09-1100-vercel-adapter-calls-the-model-twice.message.md`, deliberately not fixed.\n\nRelated: [[ptbk-browser-bundle-jsdom-task]] (same generator, `browser` field), [[promptbook-verification-step-order]]\n","numLines":29,"startLine":1,"totalLines":29}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Q5YbEzLt4PMkxS9qj2ghqM","type":"tool_result","content":"<system-reminder>This memory is 34 days old. Memories are point-in-time observations, not live state — claims about code behavior or file:line citations may be outdated. Verify against current code before asserting as fact.</system-reminder>\n1\t---\n2\tname: coder-bash-login-shell-cost\n3\tdescription: \"On this machine a Git Bash LOGIN shell costs ~9.5s (nvm in ~/.bash_profile), so every coder test that spawns a harness script pays it — the usual cause of timeout flakes in scripts/run-codex-prompts tests\"\n4\tmetadata: \n5\t  node_type: memory\n6\t  type: project\n7\t  originSessionId: a99b7a4b-c1bc-40a0-9b2a-617db763c560\n8\t  modified: 2026-08-14T10:35:16.192Z\n9\t---\n10\t\n11\tMeasured 2026-08-14 on this machine: `bash -lc 'true'` takes **~9.2–9.7 s**, while `bash -c 'true'` takes **0.13 s**.\n12\tCause is `~/.bash_profile` sourcing `nvm.sh` + nvm `bash_completion`, which is pathologically slow under Git Bash on\n13\tWindows. `bash --noprofile --norc -c 'true'` is 0.12 s, confirming the profile is the whole cost.\n14\t\n15\t`buildLoggedBashExecution` (`scripts/run-codex-prompts/common/runGoScript/scriptExecutionLog.ts`) spawns harness\n16\tscripts with `bash -lc ...` — the **only** `-lc` site in the coder runner. The `-l` is load-bearing: harness binaries\n17\t(codex/claude/gemini) live on the nvm/npm-global PATH that only the login profile sets. **Never drop `-l` to make a\n18\ttest faster.**\n19\t\n20\tConsequence: any test that spawns a real harness script pays ~10 s before its script runs a single line. Measured\n21\tend-to-end for `$spawnLoggedBashScript.test.ts`: **12.66 s from spawn to first heartbeat**, then only 1.8 s for the\n22\tactual process-tree termination being asserted.\n23\t\n24\t**Why:** this is a machine/environment cost that has nothing to do with the behavior under test, so it must be\n25\tbudgeted separately. Reusing one timeout constant for both \"wait for the fixture to boot\" and \"wait for the asserted\n26\tbehavior\" is what made `$spawnLoggedBashScript.test.ts` flake — a 20 s budget with 12.7 s already spent on shell boot\n27\tblows up as soon as a second Jest worker (`maxWorkers: 2`) competes for the disk.\n28\t\n29\t**How to apply:** when a `scripts/run-codex-prompts` test times out waiting for a spawned script, do NOT assume the\n30\tproduction logic broke — measure the startup leg first. Give setup waits a generous budget (Jest `testTimeout` is\n31\t5 minutes, so there is room) and keep the tight bound only on the assertion. Also make the wait abort early when the\n32\twrapper shell exits, printing its exit code / signal / captured output — otherwise a wrapper that dies immediately\n33\tlooks identical to a slow machine. Related: [[promptbook-jest-eperm-verification-flake]],\n34\t[[promptbook-prettier-baseline]].\n35\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8f44f218-fe4b-4504-acd8-438e13a0f15f","uuid":"2333b6b9-0e4b-4533-bbae-ce80dfaf345e","timestamp":"2026-09-17T12:34:56.940Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\.claude\\projects\\C--Users-me-work-ai-promptbook\\memory\\coder-bash-login-shell-cost.md","content":"---\nname: coder-bash-login-shell-cost\ndescription: \"On this machine a Git Bash LOGIN shell costs ~9.5s (nvm in ~/.bash_profile), so every coder test that spawns a harness script pays it — the usual cause of timeout flakes in scripts/run-codex-prompts tests\"\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: a99b7a4b-c1bc-40a0-9b2a-617db763c560\n  modified: 2026-08-14T10:35:16.192Z\n---\n\nMeasured 2026-08-14 on this machine: `bash -lc 'true'` takes **~9.2–9.7 s**, while `bash -c 'true'` takes **0.13 s**.\nCause is `~/.bash_profile` sourcing `nvm.sh` + nvm `bash_completion`, which is pathologically slow under Git Bash on\nWindows. `bash --noprofile --norc -c 'true'` is 0.12 s, confirming the profile is the whole cost.\n\n`buildLoggedBashExecution` (`scripts/run-codex-prompts/common/runGoScript/scriptExecutionLog.ts`) spawns harness\nscripts with `bash -lc ...` — the **only** `-lc` site in the coder runner. The `-l` is load-bearing: harness binaries\n(codex/claude/gemini) live on the nvm/npm-global PATH that only the login profile sets. **Never drop `-l` to make a\ntest faster.**\n\nConsequence: any test that spawns a real harness script pays ~10 s before its script runs a single line. Measured\nend-to-end for `$spawnLoggedBashScript.test.ts`: **12.66 s from spawn to first heartbeat**, then only 1.8 s for the\nactual process-tree termination being asserted.\n\n**Why:** this is a machine/environment cost that has nothing to do with the behavior under test, so it must be\nbudgeted separately. Reusing one timeout constant for both \"wait for the fixture to boot\" and \"wait for the asserted\nbehavior\" is what made `$spawnLoggedBashScript.test.ts` flake — a 20 s budget with 12.7 s already spent on shell boot\nblows up as soon as a second Jest worker (`maxWorkers: 2`) competes for the disk.\n\n**How to apply:** when a `scripts/run-codex-prompts` test times out waiting for a spawned script, do NOT assume the\nproduction logic broke — measure the startup leg first. Give setup waits a generous budget (Jest `testTimeout` is\n5 minutes, so there is room) and keep the tight bound only on the assertion. Also make the wait abort early when the\nwrapper shell exits, printing its exit code / signal / captured output — otherwise a wrapper that dies immediately\nlooks identical to a slow machine. Related: [[promptbook-jest-eperm-verification-flake]],\n[[promptbook-prettier-baseline]].\n","numLines":35,"startLine":1,"totalLines":35}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01LnQmADbnndk8Wafxa8UKNn","type":"tool_result","content":"diff --git a/changelog/_current-preversion.md b/changelog/_current-preversion.md\nindex 695a46a90..eeb5889f1 100644\n--- a/changelog/_current-preversion.md\n+++ b/changelog/_current-preversion.md\n@@ -1,3 +1,41 @@\n+-   Fixed the warnings printed while installing `ptbk`. Five of the ten `npm warn deprecated` lines were caused by\n+    Promptbook itself and are gone, and an installation resolves 96 packages fewer than before:\n+\n+    -   `crypto` was declared as a dependency, although the package of that name is only a deprecated placeholder for\n+        the Node.js built-in module. Node.js resolves `crypto` to its built-in module in every case, so the package was\n+        downloaded and warned about without ever being used by anything.\n+    -   `y-websocket-server` was declared as a dependency without being imported anywhere. The only thing which runs\n+        it, `other/y-websocket-server/y-websocket.js`, starts it through `npx`, which resolves it on its own.\n+    -   `glob-promise` is replaced by `glob` itself, which returns promises since its version 9 and no longer needs a\n+        wrapper. `glob-promise` holds `glob` at version 8, which still depends on the deprecated `inflight`, so those\n+        two warned together. All eleven call sites now go through one `findFilesByGlob` utility, which keeps the two\n+        things `glob` version 8 guaranteed and the current one does not - `/` separators on Windows and a stable\n+        alphabetical order - so nothing which reads the matched filenames had to change.\n+    -   `express-openapi-validator` is updated to a release which uses `multer` 2 instead of the deprecated `multer` 1.\n+\n+    The five remaining deprecation warnings cannot be resolved from this repository. `lodash.get` and\n+    `whatwg-encoding` are used by the newest `express-openapi-validator` and `jsdom` as well, `prebuild-install` is a\n+    dependency of `better-sqlite3` which only its version 13 drops - and that version requires Node.js 22, while\n+    Promptbook still supports Node.js 18 - and `crypto-js` and `@azure/openai` are deprecated by their authors but\n+    really used by Promptbook.\n+\n+-   Reduced what `npm audit` reports after installing `ptbk` from 48 vulnerable packages to 15, and from 3 critical\n+    advisories to none. Every version pinned by Promptbook which an advisory named is raised to a release without that\n+    advisory: `next` (which also carried the only critical advisories and brings its bundled `sharp` with it),\n+    `express` (with `body-parser`, `qs` and `path-to-regexp`), `socket.io-client` (with `engine.io-client` and `ws`),\n+    `mailparser` (with `linkify-it` and its own `nodemailer`), `@aws-sdk/client-s3` (with `fast-xml-parser`),\n+    `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `nodemailer`, `dompurify`, `jspdf` and `postcss`. None of these upgrades changes the\n+    Node.js versions Promptbook supports. `nodemailer` is the only one which crosses a major version, from 7 to 9,\n+    and Promptbook calls only its `createTransport` and `sendMail`, which those versions do not change - it is now\n+    also the same installation which `mailparser` uses.\n+\n+    What is still reported either has no fixed release at all - `showdown`, and `xlsx` inside `markitdown-ts` - or can\n+    only be fixed by an upgrade which would break something else: the fixed majors of `@ai-sdk/openai`,\n+    `@ai-sdk/google`, `@ai-sdk/deepseek` (together with `undici`) and `@vercel/blob` require Node.js 22, `localtunnel`\n+    has no release which stops using a vulnerable `axios`, and a moderate advisory on `next` with a high one on the\n+    `postcss` bundled inside it, plus `monaco-editor` with the `dompurify` bundled inside it, are only fixed by\n+    upgrades of Next.js and the Monaco editor which deserve their own change.\n+\n -   `ptbk coder` now resolves `FROM`, `IMPORT`, and `TEAM` references across local agent books before compiling coding\n     instructions. Names in `@Name` and `{Name}` match first-line book titles discovered recursively beneath the selected\n     agent's folder. `./` and `../` paths resolve from the declaring book, other paths from the --git a/changelog/_current-preversion.md b/changelog/_current-preversion.md\nindex 695a46a90..eeb5889f1 100644\n--- a/changelog/_current-preversion.md\n+++ b/changelog/_current-preversion.md\n@@ -1,3 +1,41 @@\n+-   Fixed the warnings printed while installing `ptbk`. Five of the ten `npm warn deprecated` lines were caused by\n+    Promptbook itself and are gone, and an installation resolves 96 packages fewer than before:\n+\n+    -   `crypto` was declared as a dependency, although the package of that name is only a deprecated placeholder for\n+        the Node.js built-in module. Node.js resolves `crypto` to its built-in module in every case, so the package was\n+        downloaded and warned about without ever being used by anything.\n+    -   `y-websocket-server` was declared as a dependency without being imported anywhere. The only thing which runs\n+        it, `other/y-websocket-server/y-websocket.js`, starts it through `npx`, which resolves it on its own.\n+    -   `glob-promise` is replaced by `glob` itself, which returns promises since its version 9 and no longer needs a\n+        wrapper. `glob-promise` holds `glob` at version 8, which still depends on the deprecated `inflight`, so those\n+        two warned together. All eleven call sites now go through one `findFilesByGlob` utility, which keeps the two\n+        things `glob` version 8 guaranteed and the current one does not - `/` separators on Windows and a stable\n+        alphabetical order - so nothing which reads the matched filenames had to change.\n+    -   `express-openapi-validator` is updated to a release which uses `multer` 2 instead of the deprecated `multer` 1.\n+\n+    The five remaining deprecation warnings cannot be resolved from this repository. `lodash.get` and\n+    `whatwg-encoding` are used by the newest `express-openapi-validator` and `jsdom` as well, `prebuild-install` is a\n+    dependency of `better-sqlite3` which only its version 13 drops - and that version requires Node.js 22, while\n+    Promptbook still supports Node.js 18 - and `crypto-js` and `@azure/openai` are deprecated by their authors but\n+    really used by Promptbook.\n+\n+-   Reduced what `npm audit` reports after installing `ptbk` from 48 vulnerable packages to 15, and from 3 critical\n+    advisories to none. Every version pinned by Promptbook which an advisory named is raised to a release without that\n+    advisory: `next` (which also carried the only critical advisories and brings its bundled `sharp` with it),\n+    `express` (with `body-parser`, `qs` and `path-to-regexp`), `socket.io-client` (with `engine.io-client` and `ws`),\n+    `mailparser` (with `linkify-it` and its own `nodemailer`), `@aws-sdk/client-s3` (with `fast-xml-parser`),\n+    `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `nodemailer`, `dompurify`, `jspdf` and `postcss`. None of these upgrades changes the\n+    Node.js versions Promptbook supports. `nodemailer` is the only one which crosses a major version, from 7 to 9,\n+    and Promptbook calls only its `createTransport` and `sendMail`, which those versions do not change - it is now\n+    also the same installation which `mailparser` uses.\n+\n+    What is still reported either has no fixed release at all - `showdown`, and `xlsx` inside `markitdown-ts` - or can\n+    only be fixed by an upgrade which would break something else: the fixed majors of `@ai-sdk/openai`,\n+    `@ai-sdk/google`, `@ai-sdk/deepseek` (together with `undici`) and `@vercel/blob` require Node.js 22, `localtunnel`\n+    has no release which stops using a vulnerable `axios`, and a moderate advisory on `next` with a high one on the\n+    `postcss` bundled inside it, plus `monaco-editor` with the `dompurify` bundled inside it, are only fixed by\n+    upgrades of Next.js and the Monaco editor which deserve their own change.\n+\n -   `ptbk coder` now resolves `FROM`, `IMPORT`, and `TEAM` references across local agent books before compiling coding\n     instructions. Names in `@Name` and `{Name}` match first-line book titles discovered recursively beneath the selected\n     agent's folder. `./` and `../` paths resolve from the declaring book, other paths from the leaving a test hanging indefinitely.\n */\nasync function waitForProcessToExit(commandProcess: ChildProcess): Promise<void> {\n    if (isChildProcessFinished(commandProcess)) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n        const timeout = setTimeout(() => {\n            cleanup();\n            reject(new Error('The Bash process tree did not terminate before the test timeout.'));\n        }, PROCESS_TREE_TERMINATION_TIMEOUT_MS);\n\n        const cleanup = (): void => {\n            clearTimeout(timeout);\n            commandProcess.off('exit', handleExit);\n            commandProcess.off('error', handleError);\n        };\n        const handleExit = (): void => {\n            cleanup();\n            resolve();\n        };\n        const handleError = (error: Error): void => {\n            cleanup();\n            reject(error);\n        };\n\n        commandProcess.once('exit', handleExit);\n        commandProcess.once('error', handleError);\n    });\n}\n\n/**\n * Determines whether the direct child process already exited or received a terminating signal.\n */\nfunction isChildProcessFinished(commandProcess: ChildProcess): boolean {\n    return commandProcess.exitCode !== null || commandProcess.signalCode !== null;\n}\n\n/**\n * Buffered standard streams of one test process, used to explain unexpected fixture failures.\n */\ntype CollectedProcessOutput = {\n    readonly text: string;\n};\n\n/**\n * Mirrors the standard streams of one spawned test process into a buffer.\n */\nfunction collectProcessOutput(commandProcess: ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams): CollectedProcessOutput {\n    const chunks: string[] = [];\n\n    commandProcess.stdout.on('data', (chunk) => chunks.push(chunk.toString()));\n    commandProcess.stderr.on('data', (chunk) => chunks.push(chunk.toString()));\n\n    return {\n        get text(): string {\n            return chunks.join('');\n        },\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * One started harness fixture together with the wrapper shell that owns it.\n */\ntype HarnessFixture = {\n    harnessHeartbeatPath: string;\n    bashProcess: anything, waiting for the full startup budget would only hide why, so\n * the fixture failure is reported immediately together with the output the shell produced.\n */\nasync function waitForHarnessHeartbeat({\n    harnessHeartbeatPath,\n    bashProcess,\n    bashOutput,\n}: HarnessFixture): Promise<void> {\n    const deadlineTimeMs = Date.now() + HARNESS_FIXTURE_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS;\n    const isHeartbeatWritten = async (): Promise<boolean> =>\n        Boolean((await readFile(harnessHeartbeatPath, 'utf-8').catch(() => '')).trim());\n\n    while (Date.now() < deadlineTimeMs) {\n        if (await isHeartbeatWritten()) {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        if (isChildProcessFinished(bashProcess)) {\n            // Note: The heartbeat can still land between the last check and the exit of the wrapper shell.\n            if (await isHeartbeatWritten()) {\n                return;\n            }\n\n            throw createHarnessStartupError({\n                reason: 'its wrapper shell exited first',\n                harnessHeartbeatPath,\n                bashProcess,\n                bashOutput,\n            });\n        }\n\n        await wait(FIXTURE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS);\n    }\n\n    throw createHarnessStartupError({\n        reason: `it did not start within ${HARNESS_FIXTURE_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS} ms`,\n ${harnessHeartbeatPath}\n                Wrapper shell exit code: ${bashProcess.exitCode ?? '(still running)'}\n                Wrapper shell signal: ${bashProcess.signalCode ?? '(none)'}\n\n                Wrapper shell output:\n                ${block(bashOutput.text.trim() || '(no output)')}\n            `,\n        ),\n    );\n}\n\n/**\n * Waits for one bounded test delay.\n */\nfunction wait(delayMs: number): Promise<void> {\n    return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));\n}\n","numLines":254,"startLine":1,"totalLines":254}}}

expect(log).toContain(\"printf 'runner stdout\\\\n'\");\n        expect(log).toContain('runner stdout');\n        expect(log).toContain('runner stderr');\n        expect(log).toContain('Status: 'test-package-generation', cwd: PROJECT_ROOT },\n    { script: 'test-unit', cwd: PROJECT_ROOT },\n    { script: 'lint', cwd: AGENTS_SERVER_ROOT },\n    { script: 'test-build', cwd: AGENTS_SERVER_ROOT },\n];\n\n/**\n * Runs one npm script and resolves only after the child process and its stdio streams are fully closed.\n *\n * @param {{script: string, cwd: string}} step - Verification step definition.\n * @returns {Promise<void>} Promise that resolves on success.\n */\nfunction runVerificationStep(step) {\n    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n        const childProcess = spawn(`${NPM_COMMAND} run ${step.script}`, {\n            cwd: step.cwd,\n            stdio: 'inherit',\n            env: process.env,\n            shell: true,\n        });\n\n        childProcess.on('error', (error) => {\n            reject(error);\n        });\n\n        childProcess.on('close', (code, signal) => {\n            if (code === 0) {\n                resolve();\n                return;\n            }\n\n            reject(\n                new Error(\n                    `Verification step \\`${step.script}\\` failed with code ${String(code)} and signal ${String(signal)}.`,\n                ),\n            );\n        });\n    });\n}\n\n/**\n * Executes the Promptbook Coder verification suite from the lightest checks to the heaviest build step.\n */\nasync function main() {\n    console.info('Note: Running from most lightweight to heaviest tests');\n\n    for (const step of TEST_FOR_PTBK_CODER_STEPS) {\n        await runVerificationStep(step);\n    }\n\n    console.info('🎉 All tests passed!');\n}\n\nvoid main().catch((error) => {\n    console.error(error instanceof Error ? error.message : error);\n    process.exitCode = 1;\n});\n","numLines":88,"startLine":1,"totalLines":88}}}
