Publishing to the Visual Studio Code Marketplace is available through `npm run build:vscode-extension -- --publish`, which generates the grammar, syncs a Marketplace-safe extension version from the root `package.json`, publishes with `vsce`, and creates the VSIX artifact.\n\n-   Fixed `<BookEditor/>` syntax highlighting incorrectly highlighting the local part of email addresses (e.g. `team@foo.bar`) as agent references. `@`-style references now require whitespace or start-of-line before the `@` sign, so only `@Paul` (with preceding whitespace) is highlighted, not `team@foo.bar`. Removed a now-redundant manual preceding-character check that duplicated this logic.\n\n-   Improved `<BookEditor/>` syntax highlighting to dynamically detect commitments — any line starting with one or more all-uppercase words (minimum 2 characters each) is now highlighted as a commitment keyword, without relying on a hardcoded list of known commitment types. Lines starting with a dash or a single uppercase letter are not affected. Special commitment types (`NOTE`, `NOTES`, `NONCE`, `TODO`) retain their distinct colors, and `FROM`/`IMPORT`/`IMPORTS`/`TEAM` retain agent-reference link highlighting.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server VPS installation failing on the first run with a Node.js out-of-memory crash during the Next.js production build. The `ptbk agents-server build` command now passes `--max-old-space-size=4096` in `NODE_OPTIONS` when spawning the webpack compilation process, allowing the ~1.9 GiB peak heap usage to succeed within the swap-backed memory budget enforced by the installer. Existing `NODE_OPTIONS` values are preserved; the flag is only injected when no `--max-old-space-size` is already set.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server file upload URLs for self-contained S3 to hide the internal bucket name, path prefix, and directory structure. Files are now stored under a content-addressed key (`{hash[0]}/{hash[1]}/{sha256}/{filename}`) and served through a new Next.js proxy route (`/s3/{hex}/{hex}/{hash}/{filename}`) so the public URL is unguessable and reveals no internal storage details. Old-style URLs (e.g. `/s3/promptbook-files/ptbk-agents/user/files/…`) remain accessible for backwards compatibility.\n\n-   Fixed citation source previews in Agents Server chat failing silently when the target page blocks iframe embedding via `X-Frame-Options` (e.g. `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`). The chat modal now checks embeddability server-side before rendering and falls back to a server-taken screenshot with an \"Open in new tab\" link when the page cannot be framed.\n\n-   Optimized Agents Server database layer to prevent the server from becoming unresponsive under load:\n\n    -   Added `connectionTimeoutMillis` (15 s) to the shared PostgreSQL connection pool so queries fail fast when all connections are busy instead of queuing indefinitely — the root cause of the server becoming completely unresponsive after a period of high traffic.\n    -   Increased the default pool size from 10 to 20 connections (configurable via `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` environment variable) to handle more concurrent chat-stream polling and atomic-SQL operations without exhausting the pool.\n    -   Added `idleTimeoutMillis` (30 s) and `allowExitOnIdle` so unused connections are closed promptly, keeping memory and socket usage low.\n    -   Added a pool `error` event handler so unexpected errors on idle clients are logged instead of propagating as unhandled exceptions that can corrupt the pool state.\n    -   Added a 30-second hard timeout to every Supabase HTTP request via a custom `fetch` wrapper on the server-side Supabase client. Without this, a slow or temporarily unreachable PostgREST endpoint would cause Supabase queries to hang indefinitely, holding Node.js event-loop resources and contributing to the gradual unresponsiveness over time.\n\n-   Added `isVerbose` option to `CliAgent` so callers can enable the same harness-level console output that `ptbk agent exec --verbose` produces without spawning the CLI. `LiteAgent` already supported `isVerbose`; both classes now expose the option consistently.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat runner not including the agent's initial message (defined via `INITIAL MESSAGE` commitment) in the queued book file when a user sends their first message. The local and external chat runners now prepend the agent's initial message as the opening `MESSAGE @Agent` block so the agent runner sees the full conversation context from the start.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat messages being silently cropped when the agent response contained a line starting with a single uppercase ASCII letter followed by lowercase text (e.g. \"V části...\" in Czech). `Book.parse` was incorrectly treating such lines as commitment headers due to an overly permissive regex in `parseCommitmentHeader`. The fix tightens the regex to require at least two characters in the first keyword word, which prevents common natural-language words like \"V\" (Czech for \"in\") or \"A\" / \"I\" in English from being mistaken for commitment markers.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server chat tray ordering from last-activity time to creation time so chats stay in their chronological position and browsing an older chat no longer moves it to the top of the list.\n\n-   Optimized animated avatar rendering performance in Agents Server to fix 1–2 fps drops when multiple avatars are visible:\n\n    -   Throttled the shared animation loop to ~24 fps (from the display refresh rate of 60 fps+) via a frame-interval gate in `avatarAnimationScheduler.ts`. Animated octopus visuals change slowly enough that 24 fps is perceptually identical to 60 fps while reducing total render work by ~60%.\n    -   Cached stable per-avatar data (morphology profile, animation phase, tentacle profiles, eye phase offsets) using a `WeakMap` keyed on the `createRandom` factory reference in `octopus3dAvatarVisual`, `octopus3d2AvatarVisual`, and `octopus3d3AvatarVisual`. These values are deterministic given the avatar definition and were previously recomputed on every frame.\n    -   Replaced `context.filter = 'blur()'` shadow effects in all six affected visuals (`octopus3d`, `octopus3d2`, `octopus3d3`, `minecraft`, `minecraft2`, `fractal`) with equivalent gradient-based approximations. CSS filter blur forces the browser into a full software rasterization pass on every frame; the gradient alternative is hardware-accelerated and visually equivalent.\n    -   Added `\"ts-node\": { \"transpileOnly\": true }` to `tsconfig.json` so the CLI integration test (`ts-node src/cli/test/ptbk.ts --help`) skips full type-checking during execution. Type correctness is still enforced by the dedicated `test-types` step; this change brings the CLI startup from an uncapped compile pass (> 5 min on Windows) down to ~20 seconds.\n\n-   Further optimized animated avatar rendering performance in Agents Server, building on the earlier 24 fps throttle and stable-state cache. With twelve animated octopus avatars on a single page the previous pass still left the UI at 1–2 fps because every visible avatar fired on the same animation frame and the per-frame mesh sampling cost remained heavy:\n\n    -   Interleaved listeners in `avatarAnimationScheduler.ts` so animated avatars no longer all render on the same animation frame. Each listener now tracks its own last-run timestamp, new listeners are phase-staggered at registration, and the shared loop runs at most `MAX_AVATAR_LISTENERS_PER_FRAME` (= 2) listeners per `requestAnimationFrame`, scheduling the rest on subsequent frames. Each avatar still reaches the 24 fps target individually; total per-frame work is bounded regardless of how many avatars are visible.\n    -   Added per-frame corner-grid sample caching to `octopus3d3AvatarVisual` and `octopus3d2AvatarVisual`. The mesh patch loop previously called `sampleContinuousOctopusSurfacePoint` / `sampleBlobbyOctopusSurfacePoint` for each of the four corners of every patch (16×40×4 = 2 560 samples per frame for `octopus3d3`), even though most corners are shared between neighboring patches. The new implementation precomputes a `(latitudePatchCount + 1) × (longitudePatchCount + 1)` corner grid once per frame, cutting the sample call count by ~3.7× on `octopus3d3` and ~4× on `octopus3d2`.\n    -   Added per-frame longitude caching for `resolveContinuousTentacleInfluence`, `resolveContinuousLobeWave`, and `resolveLowerLobeWave` in the same two visuals. Each tentacle-influence evaluation runs an 8-iteration `Math.exp` loop over the seeded tentacle profiles, so calling it once per longitude grid value instead of once per corner cuts the dominant inner-loop cost by ~30×. The new `sampleContinuousOctopusSurfacePointWithLongitudeCache` / `sampleBlobbyOctopusSurfacePointWithLongitudeCache` helpers accept the cached values explicitly; the existing public sample functions are preserved for off-grid callers (eyes, mouth).\n\n-   Added `--wait [duration]` flag to `ptbk coder run` for controlling the delay between prompt rounds:\n\n    -   `--wait 1h` (or `--wait 30m`, `--wait 5s`, combinations like `--wait 1h30m`) waits the specified duration between rounds to avoid hitting harness rate limits. The first prompt executes immediately; the wait is inserted only before subsequent rounds.\n    -   `--wait` without a value retains the existing interactive behavior — waits for user confirmation before each prompt.\n    -   No flag (or `--no-wait`) means no waiting, which is now the default. `--no-wait` is kept for backward compatibility.\n\n-   Fixed `CliAgent` failing with `Missing --harness in non-dry run mode` when no `harness` is provided: `CliAgent` now falls back to the `PTBK_HARNESS` environment variable, mirroring `ptbk agent exec` behavior. Similarly falls back to `PTBK_MODEL` and `PTBK_THINKING_LEVEL` env vars. Extracted shared env-var constants (`PTBK_HARNESS_ENV`, `PTBK_MODEL_ENV`, `PTBK_THINKING_LEVEL_ENV`), harness names (`CLI_AGENT_HARNESS_NAMES`), and thinking-level values (`CLI_AGENT_THINKING_LEVEL_VALUES`) into the new `src/book-3.0/cliAgentEnv.ts` so CLI and library share a single source of truth. readability and maintainability.\n-   Fix width of the message in the chat by adding a minimum width and improving layout for short messages.\n-   Use model `gemini-3-pro-image-preview` for the agent of Avatar Images\n-   Updated `openai` from `4.63.0` to `6.18.0` and fixed all resulting type errors.\n-   Resolved `zod` peer dependency conflicts between `@ai-sdk/deepseek` and `@openai/agents` by using `overrides` in `package.json`.\n-   Fixed `node-fetch` declaration issue in `LindatAutomaticTranslator.ts` by using native `URLSearchParams` and removing `node-fetch` import.\n-   Stabilized Agents Server under low traffic by removing constant 5-second DB polling from timeout/preparation workers, restoring durable timeout wake-ups through Vercel cron, fixing agent-source cycle detection across canonical/name URLs, and reducing agent-reference resolver churn.\n-   Logged richer durable diagnostics for failed Agents Server chat turns so admin task inspection no longer stops at the generic lease-expired summary:\n\n    -   Added backwards-compatible `failureDetails` storage for `UserChatJob` rows and now persist structured JSON diagnostics containing the failure summary, serialized error payload (message/name/stack when available), provider, timing, and chat-turn identifiers.\n    -   Reused the same diagnostics builder for runtime failures, unexpected worker-route failures, and expired-lease recovery paths to keep failure logging DRY and consistent.\n    -   Extended the admin task manager to surface the stored diagnostics under failed chat-completion tasks via an expandable \"Show details\" panel in the Last error column.\n\n-   Refactored Agents Server `apps/agents-server/src/app/agents/[agentName]/api/chat/route.ts` into smaller focused private chat-route helpers without changing external behavior:\n\n    -   Moved request-time runtime assembly, disclaimer and credential resolution, history initialization, and frozen team-member chat persistence behind the private `resolveAgentChatRouteContext` and `createTeamMemberFrozenChatPersistence` facades so `route.ts` now reads as a thin HTTP entrypoint.\n    -   Extracted the long-lived markdown stream orchestration, cancellation handling, tool-call framing, and final post-processing into the private `createAgentChatStreamResponse` helper while preserving the existing stateless chat streaming behavior, keep-alives, history recording, learning, and calendar activity logging.\n\n-   Enhanced the Agents Server new-agent wizard team step so it now behaves as a homepage-style multi-select picker:\n\n    -   Removed the separate manual \"Team members\" entry UI and kept only the existing-agents picker headed by \"Browse existing agents\" / \"Vyberte existující agenty\".\n    -   Kept multi-selection for teammate agents across the local server and federated servers while continuing to exclude the hidden core server from federated lists.\n    -   Extracted a shared homepage-like `AgentCardsSection` renderer so the wizard and federated-agent surfaces reuse the same card-grid, loading, empty, and error presentation.\n\n-   Improved Agents Server expired chat-worker diagnostics so the stale \"Background worker lease expired before the chat turn finished.\" failure now leaves actionable evidence instead of a generic summary:\n\n    -   Added shared expired-lease diagnostics for durable chat jobs that record queue/run/heartbeat timing, worker runtime thresholds, configured server limits, and a snapshot of active chat jobs and timeouts at the moment recovery runs.\n    -   Started logging structured `lease_expired` recovery/reconciliation events so server logs show which background tasks were active and whether the job had already outlived the 300-second worker route limit when heartbeats stopped.\n\n-   Added immediate optimistic profile-to-chat navigation in Agents Server, so starting a first message from an agent profile now swaps to the chat route without waiting for the server and keeps the user bubble visible throughout the handoff:\n\n    -   Persisted profile-to-chat optimistic turn metadata across the route transition, including the client message id reused later for canonical reconciliation and failure states.\n    -   Added a chat-route loading surface that renders the pending user turn right away while the standalone chat page server data is still loading.\n    -   Tightened optimistic/canonical merge ordering so unresolved user bubbles stay ahead of later assistant streaming messages until the server confirms them.\n\n-   Added the new deterministic `AsciiOctopus` avatar visual alongside the existing avatar set, with an animated ASCII-art rendering that keeps the same organic alien octopus feel as `Octopus3` while varying its blob silhouette, tentacle count, face, and colors from the agent name, hash, colors, and animation time:\n\n    -   Added the new built-in `ascii-octopus` canvas renderer to the shared avatar registry without changing the existing `Octopus`, `Octopus2`, `Octopus3`, pixel-art, Minecraft, or Fractal visuals.\n    -   Kept the implementation DRY by reusing shared octopus body and tentacle geometry helpers, while translating that geometry into deterministic ASCII glyphs instead of painted surfaces.\n    -   Updated the existing utils `/avatars` playground and regression coverage so the new renderer appears in the selector, preview grid, deterministic sample gallery, and supported URL-state parsing without creating a separate page.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server metadata enum handling so predefined metadata keys no longer accept arbitrary strings in `/admin/metadata`:\n\n    -   Added shared metadata definitions with reusable predefined option lists, so enum-like metadata such as `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL`, `SERVER_LANGUAGE`, `SERVER_VISIBILITY`, `CHAT_FEEDBACK_MODE`, `CHAT_VISUAL_MODE`, `NAME_POOL`, `DEFAULT_VISIBILITY`, and `NEW_AGENT_WIZARD` now render as selects instead of free-form text inputs.\n    -   Reused the same option registries across the metadata page and existing server-creation flows to keep enum values centralized and DRY.\n    -   Added server-side validation for predefined metadata options, so invalid enum values are rejected even when `/api/metadata` is called directly.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk agent-folder run` / `ptbk agent-folder tick` with the GitHub Copilot runner on Windows/MSYS for large queued-message prompts:\n\n    -   Stopped passing the full generated agent prompt as one `copilot -p \"...\"` shell argument, which could exceed the shell/Node argument-length limit and fail with `Argument list too long`.\n    -   Switched the GitHub Copilot runner to feed prompts through standard input instead, keeping `--model`, `--reasoning-effort`, and the existing non-interactive flags unchanged.\n    -   Added regression coverage for the new stdin-based invocation shape so agent-mode prompts stay safe even when the Book Language blueprint makes them much larger than coder prompts.\n\n-   Enhanced the `ptbk agent-folder run` rich terminal UI so it now reflects queued-message workflows instead of mirroring `ptbk coder run`:\n\n    -   The top branding now uses compact initials derived from the local `agent.book` title, making the dashboard identify the actual agent definition rather than only the runner selected by `--harness`.\n    -   The session summary now distinguishes the local agent from the execution runner and shows queue-specific totals (`finished` / `queued` / total) with a progress bar based on answered messages instead of `Task 1/1`.\n    -   Added a dedicated `User message` box that shows the latest `MESSAGE @User` block 1:1 with line-preserving trimming, while keeping the live streaming output panel unchanged.\n\n-   Enhanced the `ptbk agent-folder run` terminal dashboard so long-running agent sessions stay inside one stable rich UI:\n\n    -   Kept a single persistent boxed UI alive across queued-message runs, moving idle watching and idle auto-pull activity into explicit in-frame `WAITING` / loading states instead of printing plain lines that broke the layout mid-session.\n    -   Changed the header visual to render the local agent name in a smaller compact banner instead of large initials, while keeping the rest of the terminal frame layout intact.\n    -   Kept the queued-thread preview focused on the latest `MESSAGE @User` from the `.book` thread via `src/book-3.0/Book.ts`, and deferred the coding-agent Git identity tip until process exit so it no longer interrupts active sessions or `--no-ui` streaming output.\n\n-   Refactored `OpenAiAssistantExecutionTools` internals to keep OpenAI Assistants behavior unchanged while making the module easier to follow and maintain:\n\n    -   Split `src/llm-providers/openai/OpenAiAssistantExecutionTools.ts` into a smaller orchestration facade plus focused private helpers for prompt/thread building, tool-run execution, streaming/result reporting, and citation rewriting.\n    -   Kept assistant chat execution, tool progress streaming, hosted tool invocation, file attachment handling, assistant creation/update flows, and final Promptbook result export behavior unchanged while reducing the responsibility count inside the top-level file.\n\n-   Fixed the self-contained Stalwart mail server of Agents Server, which rejected every management call and therefore never routed inbound or outbound agent mail:\n\n    -   Fixed `install.sh`, which decided that Stalwart was already bootstrapped whenever `/etc/stalwart/config.json` existed. Stalwart writes that file itself - it is only its storage descriptor, for example `{\"@type\":\"RocksDb\",\"path\":\"/var/lib/stalwart/\",...}` - already during its very first startup, long before anything is bootstrapped, and never touches it again. The installer therefore skipped the `x:Bootstrap/set` call on **every** fresh installation and left the mail server permanently in bootstrap mode, where it refuses every management call with `{\"type\":\"forbidden\",\"description\":\"The server is in bootstrap mode. ...\"}`. The bootstrap state is now read from Stalwart itself through a management probe, so a pending bootstrap is completed on the next installer run and an already bootstrapped server is left untouched.\n    -   Fixed the Stalwart management payloads, which sent JSON arrays for `aliases`, `credentials`, `memberGroupIds`, `stages`, and the MTA hook `enable.match` expression, while Stalwart serializes every `set` / `objectList` property as an object and answered `invalidPatch` / `Invalid value for object property`. Added shared `toStalwartJmapSet` and `toStalwartJmapObjectList` helpers so all payloads build these shapes in one place.\n    -   Fixed `install.sh`, which provisioned the Agents Server Stalwart administrator inside the reserved `promptbook.invalid` domain. Stalwart rejects such a domain as an `Invalid domain name`, so the step failed and, because of `set -Eeuo pipefail`, aborted the whole installation before nginx, firewall, and certificate configuration ever ran. The bootstrap-time administrator credentials are now kept as Stalwart's fixed `STALWART_RECOVERY_ADMIN` credentials instead of provisioning a second administrator account.\n    -   Fixed the Stalwart step of `install.sh` aborting the whole installation when the mail server cannot be bootstrapped. Because `configure_firewall`, `configure_nginx_reverse_proxy`, and `configure_ssl_certificates` all run afterwards, a mail server problem used to leave the VPS without a firewall, reverse proxy, or certificates. The step now warns and continues, and the bootstrap is retried by every later installer run.\n    -   Fixed outbound submission, which was configured for port `587`, a port a bootstrapped Stalwart never opens. Agents Server now submits through `submissions` on port `465` with implicit TLS, and the email server administration pages document that port instead of `587`.\n    -   Fixed the catch-all address being assigned before the mailbox behind it existed, so synchronizing an already-known domain no longer fails on its first management call.\n    -   Improved Stalwart error reporting so a rejected object now includes Stalwart's own `notCreated` / `notUpdated` reason, and a server still in **bootstrap mode** reports an actionable message instead of a raw `forbidden` response.\n    -   Fixed the `promptbook-agents-server` build, which loaded the Next.js command line interface through the hardcoded path `../../node_modules/next/dist/bin/next`. That path does not exist inside a git worktree without its own installed dependencies, such as the `ptbk coder --isolate` worktrees, so `npm run build` failed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` even though Next.js was resolvable. The new `apps/agents-server/scripts/next-cli.js` resolves it through Node's own module resolution instead.\n\n-   Fixed the self-contained Stalwart mail server staying unusable whenever its initial setup was left pending. Completing that setup used to be the sole responsibility of `install.sh`, so a mail server which was installed before the bootstrap fix - or whose bootstrap failed once - answered every management call with `{\"type\":\"forbidden\",\"description\":\"The server is in bootstrap mode. ...\"}`, and **Synchronize Stalwart** on `/admin/email-server` could only report the error, never resolve it. Because the VPS self-update runs the _deployed_ release's installer, such a server stayed broken for at least one more update cycle. Agents Server now completes the bootstrap itself as the first step of every domain synchronization, which happens on startup and on **Synchronize Stalwart**, and it asks Stalwart for its bootstrap state instead of inferring it from files on disk. The setup Stalwart receives - mail hostname, default domain, automatic DKIM keys, and no ACME certificate request because nginx and certbot own every certificate on the VPS - is now defined by `buildStalwartBootstrapValue`, which `install.sh` mirrors under the shared `[📬]` marker because a fresh VPS is bootstrapped before Agents Server is built, and the result is verified against Stalwart itself so a bootstrap that was accepted but not applied is reported with the remaining manual step instead of a raw `forbidden` response. The installer keeps performing the bootstrap for a fresh installation and additionally waits until Stalwart really left bootstrap mode after the restart it needs to open its mail listeners, so the first synchronization of a newly started Agents Server no longer races a mail server that is still coming up.\n-   Improved the Agents Server **Book language manual** so its linked table of contents navigates directly to each commitment, and each end-to-end example links its used commitments back to their sections. The manual now describes `@Foo` and `{Foo foo}` as agent references rather than parameters, renames the `---` primitive to **Multiple agent**, documents code fences as ` ``` `, links every generated-from source to the Promptbook repository, hides parser/runtime implementation details and unfinished commitments, and keeps each commitment example focused on its canonical keyword with only `GOAL` and `CLOSED` as supporting syntax.\n\n-   Fixed the published `@promptbook/components` package, which broke the production build of every browser application that installs `ptbk`, `promptbook` or `@promptbook/components`. Rendered markdown is sanitized by `DOMPurify`, which needs a DOM, so `renderMarkdown` creates one through `jsdom` whenever it runs outside of a browser - for example during server-side rendering. That code path is unreachable in a browser, but bundlers resolve `require('jsdom')` statically, so `next build` followed it into `jsdom` and failed with **Module not found: Can't resolve `fs`** together with the same error for `child_process` and `net`. It failed even for an application that imports `<MarkdownContent/>` with `ssr: false`, because a bundler resolves a module it will never execute just as eagerly as one it will:\n\n    -   The generated manifest of every package that is not Node-only now declares `\"browser\": { \"jsdom\": false }`, which is the standard way to tell a browser bundler to replace a Node-only dependency with an empty module. Browser builds therefore no longer follow `jsdom` (and no longer ship it), while Node.js ignores the `browser` field and keeps resolving the real library for server-side rendering. The stubs are derived from the dependencies which the generated package really has, so a Node-only dependency which appears in a browser-facing package in the future is covered without another manual change.\n    -   Creating the server-side DOM moved from `renderMarkdown` into `$provideServerDomWindow`, which is now the single place where browser-facing code touches `jsdom`. A runtime that can provide neither the DOM of a browser nor `jsdom` is now reported as a branded `EnvironmentMismatchError` explaining why markdown can not be sanitized, instead of failing with `JSDOM is not a constructor`.\n    -   The list of Node-only packages is now shared through `isNodeOnlyPackage` between the publish-safety check and the dependency step of the package generation, instead of being written down twice.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":15,"oldLines":9,"newStart":15,"newLines":9,"lines":[" ","     The five remaining deprecation warnings cannot be resolved from this repository. `lodash.get` and","     `whatwg-encoding` are used by the newest `express-openapi-validator` and `jsdom` as well, `prebuild-install` is a","-    dependency of `better-sqlite3` which only its version 13 drops - and that version requires Node.js 22, while","-    Promptbook still supports Node.js 18 - and `crypto-js` and `@azure/openai` are deprecated by their authors but","-    really used by Promptbook.","+    dependency of `better-sqlite3` which only its version 13 drops - and that version requires Node.js 22, while the","+    `engines` of Promptbook still allow Node.js 18 - and `crypto-js` and `@azure/openai` are deprecated by their","+    authors but really used by Promptbook."," "," -   Reduced what `npm audit` reports after installing `ptbk` from 48 vulnerable packages to 15, and from 3 critical","     advisories to none. Every version pinned by Promptbook which an advisory named is raised to a release without that"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

## Your Behavior

You are Promptbook Developer
You are a helpful, honest, and intelligent AI assistant. Your goal is to provide accurate, clear, and concise responses while being friendly and engaging. Think step-by-step before answering complex questions.

### Rules

-   If you're unsure about something, say so and offer to look it up or clarify.
-   You can use Markdown formatting in the messages like **bold** or *italic*
-   You can use Markdown code blocks if needed

For example:

```javascript
console.log('Hello');
```
-   Keep in mind the DRY _(don't repeat yourself)_ principle.
-   Keep in mind the SOLID principles.
-   Do a proper analysis of the current functionality before you start implementing.
-   Keep small responsibilities of functions and classes, avoid creating big functions or classes that do many things.
-   When throwing errors, throw [branded errors](src/errors) and use `spaceTrim` utility to write clear and well-formatted multiline detailed error messages.

Output Format: errors as markdown, for example `variables` should be in backticks and important notes can be in bold.
-   Constants should always be `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`.
-   Boolean variables should always be prefixed with `is`, for example `isUserChatJobLeaseExpired` or `IS_DEBUG_MODE`.
-   Do not use abbreviations, for example use `isExpired` instead of `isExp`, `translateMessage` instead of `t`, etc.
It is fine to use well-known abbreviations, for example `id`, `url`, `html`, etc.
-   When writing multiline strings, use `spaceTrim` utility.
-   Do only the change described in the prompt. Do not add any additional features or make any additional changes that are not described there.
If you find some critical issue that is not described in the prompt, report it to `agents-messages` in the root of the project.

## Context

### How to Contribute

-   **Add changes in [Changelog](/changelog/_current-preversion.md)**
-   **Test your changes** to ensure they work as expected, use `npm test`

### Code Style

-   Follow the existing code style and structure.
-   Use comments to explain complex logic.

### Emoji in `[brackets]`

-   `[any emoji]` Connects multiple places that are related to each other across the repository
-   `[number]` Connects multiple places that are related to each other across the file
-   `[🧠]` Marks a place where there is something to decide and think about.
-   `[🕕]` List of models _(that should be progresively updated)_
    -   Prompt: Update available models and their prices, search online
-   `[🔼]` Marks an entity (function, class, type,...) in other project (like Promptbook.studio) which should be moved to this repository
-   `[🚉]` Marks an types / interfaces / structures fully serializable as JSON, not marking `string_` and `number_` prefixed aliases
-   `[🧹]` Need to implement garbage collection
-   `[🐣]` Easter eggs
-   `[💩]` Shitty code that needs refactoring
-   `$` When entity (function, class) starts by `$`, it means it is not pure and can have side effects.
-   3x `!` Marks a place that needs to be fixed before releasing a pre-release version.
-   4x (and more) `!` Marks a place that needs to be fixed as soon as possible.
-   `@@@` Marks a place where text / documentation / ... must be written.
-   [⚫] Code in this file should never be published in any package
-   [🟢] Code in this file should never be published into packages that could be imported into browser environment
-   [🔵] Code in this file should never be published outside of `@promptbook/browser`
-   [🟡] Code in this file should never be published outside of `@promptbook/cli`
-   [💞] Ignore a discrepancy between file name and entity name

### Generated code

Across the repository, there are several places where code has been generated automatically.
Do not edit these places manually, as they will be overwritten by the code generation process. Edit the source files instead.

> ⚠️ WARNING: This code has been generated so that any manual changes will be overwritten

### Dictionary

-   **Promptbook Engine vs. Agent Server** sre two distinct parts you should know the difference:
    -   **Promptbook Engine** is the core engine that powers AI agents, it is located in `/src` folder. It is framework-agnostic and can be used in different applications. It can run as standalone javascript/typescript library, CLI environment, or be integrated into different applications. It can be also runned in Agent Server:
    -   **Agent Server** is a specific application that uses the Promptbook Engine to provide a web and API interface for creating and interacting with AI agents. It is located in `/apps/agents-server` folder.
-   **Commitments** are basic syntax elements that add specific functionalities to AI agents
    -   They are used in `agentSource`, there are commitments like `PERSONA`, `RULE`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE CALENDAR`, `USE PROJECT`, `META IMAGE`, etc.
    -   Commitments are in the folder `/src/commitments`
    -   Each commitment starts with a keyword, e.g., `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE PROJECT`, etc. on a begining of the line and end by new co
    -   Agent source with commitments is parsed by two functions:
        -   `parseAgentSource` which is a lightweight parser for agent source, it parses basic information and its purpose is to be quick and synchronous. The commitments there are hardcoded.
        -   `createAgentModelRequirements` which is an asynchronous function that creates model requirements it applies each commitment one by one and works asynchronously.

### Common rules

-   Always analyze the context and requirements before generating any code.
-   Write clear, maintainable, and well-documented code.
-   Write JSDoc comments for all entities - functions, classes, types, top-level constants, etc.
    -   When this entity is exported from the file and it is under `src` folder _(not for example in the `apps` folder)_, it must be marked either as `@public` or `@private` at the end of the JSDoc comment.
    -   For example: "@private internal utility of <Chat/>" / "@public exported from `@promptbook/browser`"
    -   If you don't know, prefer to mark it as private, we can always change it to public later, but changing from public to private may cause breaking changes.
-   You (the AI coding agent) are running inside a Node process, so do not kill all Node processes such as `taskkill /F /IM node.exe`. If you need to stop something you spawned, kill only that specific process, for example by PID or by port.

### Additional context

-   Look at attached images if there are present
-   Attached images are in folder `prompts` on the root of the project
    -   For example the ![alt text](screenshots/foo.png) is image file `prompts/screenshots/foo.png`

#### Agents server installed on VPS _(as additional context)_

-   There are two distinct things:
    1. Entire VPS
    2. Each server
-   On one VPS there can be multiple servers and each server has its own domain
-   Most things (like agents, projects, metadata, etc.) are living on each server and some things (like environment variables, superadmin, etc.) are bound to entire VPS
-   Purpose of this is to be able to run multiple clients on one VPS and each client can have its own server with its own domain and settings
-   The entire VPS is managed by superadmin and each server is managed by normal admin of that server _(or superadmin can also manage each server)_
-   Superadmin has always name `admin` and password hardcoded in environment variable `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
-   The VPS is installed by running [the `install.sh`](install.sh) script on a fresh VPS
-   Servers can be added and removed by superadmin on `/superadmin/servers` page

#### The Agents Server menu _(as additional context)_

The menu of the agent server looks like this:

1. The navigation hierarchy
    - Icon and Server name _(for example Promptbook Agents Server)_
    - arrow ">" and Agents or picked agent name (organized in folders)
    - arrow ">" and the view Profile / Chat / Book of the agent or nothing if no agent is picked
2. The menu items
    - Documentation
    - System
3. Control panel and user menu
    - Control panel
    - User menu with the avatar and the name of the user

#### Database migrations for Agents server _(as additional context)_

-   Migrations are located in `apps/agents-server/src/database/migrations`
-   Be aware that table names in migrations have prefix `prefix_` _(look at existing migrations for reference)_
-   Migrations should be backwards compatible:
    -   Meaning that earlier versions of the server should be able to run with the database after migration without any issues.
    -   This is important because we want to have the same database for production and preview environments.
    -   This database will be migrated to the latest version of the preview environment, but the production environment should be able to run with it without any issues.
    -   The only thing that can happen is that older versions of the server will not be able to use new features.
    -   Adding new columns, tables, etc. is fine, but do not remove or rename existing ones, and do not change the meaning of existing columns or tables.
    -   When in doubt, prefer to add new things instead of changing existing ones.

#### Metadata of Agents server _(as additional context)_

-   There is a table called `Metadata`.
-   It has `key` and `value` fields.
-   It is a similar concept to configuration, but this configuration can be changed by administrators in the Agents Server website.

#### Book Language blueprint _(as additional context)_

Book language is a domain-specific language used for defining AI agents in the Promptbook Engine and Agents server.
It has lightweight syntax and keywords (the commitments) that allow you to define the "soul" of the agent.
The book language is designed to be human-readable and easy to write, while also being powerful enough to express complex agent behaviors.

Every agent has its source defined in the book language, which is called "agent source". The agent source is parsed and processed by the Promptbook Engine to create the actual AI agent that can interact with users and perform tasks.
This agent source is internally converted to a structured format called "agent model requirements" which are the actual raw technical instructions for the AI model to run the agent.

There is a standalone book language documentation on each agent server on `/api/docs/book.md` route, for example `https://live.ptbk.io/api/docs/book-language.md?language=en`.
Use it as a reference for the syntax and semantics of the book language, and modify `apps/agents-server/src/utils/bookLanguageDocumentation/createStandaloneBookLanguageMarkdown.ts` if it is relevant to the change you are doing.

##### Commitments _(as additional context and part of Book Language)_

Commitments are basic syntax elements that add specific functionalities to AI agents written in `book` language.

-   They are used in `agentSource`, there are commitments like `PERSONA`, `RULE`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE CALENDAR`, `USE PROJECT`, `META IMAGE`, `CLOSED`, etc.
-   They are in the folder `src/commitments`.
-   Each commitment starts with a keyword, e.g. `PERSONA`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE PROJECT`, etc. on a beginning of the line and ends by a new commitment or the end of the book.
-   There is a general pattern that the commitment keyword is followed by a space and then by the content of the commitment, for example:
    -   `PERSONA You are a helpful assistant that helps with cooking recipes.`
    -   `USE MCP https://mcp.example.com/server`
-   In the commitment context, you can reference external agents, for example:
    -   `TEAM You can talk to {Criminal lawyer} and {Financial advisor}`

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cf9HwiMS4SomhGNadVdCs","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01DLcheSCsCsLoGcKMRSHm62","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"C:\\Users\\me\\.claude\\projects\\C--Users-me-work-ai-promptbook\\memory\\coder-bash-login-shell-cost.md","old_string":"Measured 2026-08-14 on this machine: `bash -lc 'true'` takes **~9.2–9.7 s**, while `bash -c 'true'` takes 0.13 s.\nCause is `~/.bash_profile` sourcing `nvm.sh` + nvm `bash_completion`, which is pathologically slow under Git Bash on\nWindows. `bash --noprofile --norc -c 'true'` is 0.12 s, confirming the profile is the whole cost.","new_string":"Measured 2026-08-14 on this machine: `bash -lc 'true'` takes **~9.2–9.7 s**, while `bash -c 'true'` takes 0.13 s.\nCause is `~/.bash_profile` sourcing `nvm.sh` + nvm `bash_completion`, which is pathologically slow under Git Bash on\nWindows. `bash --noprofile --norc -c 'true'` is 0.12 s, confirming the profile is the whole cost.\n\n**Re-measured 2026-09-17: the cost has quadrupled.** `bash -lc 'true'` is now **40–50 s** (three consecutive runs:\n40.4 s, 49.0 s, 49.7 s), of which ~33 s is sourcing `nvm.sh` alone and ~2.8 s is bare\n`bash --noprofile --norc -c 'true'` - so even raw Git Bash process creation got ~20x slower. This is machine-wide\n(heavy Chrome / VS Code load), not repo-caused. **Treat any such number baked into a test comment as a snapshot, not\na constant**, and re-measure before concluding that a spawn-a-shell test regressed. Same day, the 90 s startup budget\nin `$spawnLoggedBashScript.test.ts` was raised to 240 s plus a derived per-test `it(...)` timeout, because the global\nJest `testTimeout` (5 min) would otherwise cut the test off before its own explanatory error could fire. That test\ncosts ~9-15 s in isolation and >90 s inside a full `test-unit` run - the gap is the second Jest worker, so always\nreproduce this class of failure with the **whole** suite, never the single file.","originalFile":"---\nname: coder-bash-login-shell-cost\ndescription: \"On this machine a Git Bash LOGIN shell costs ~9.5s (nvm in ~/.bash_profile), so every coder test that spawns a harness script pays it — the usual cause of timeout flakes in scripts/run-codex-prompts tests\"\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: a99b7a4b-c1bc-40a0-9b2a-617db763c560\n  modified: 2026-08-14T10:35:16.192Z\n---\n\nMeasured 2026-08-14 on this machine: `bash -lc 'true'` takes **~9.2–9.7 s**, while `bash -c 'true'` takes **0.13 s**.\nCause is `~/.bash_profile` sourcing `nvm.sh` + nvm `bash_completion`, which is pathologically slow under Git Bash on\nWindows. `bash --noprofile --norc -c 'true'` is 0.12 s, confirming the profile is the whole cost.\n\n`buildLoggedBashExecution` (`scripts/run-codex-prompts/common/runGoScript/scriptExecutionLog.ts`) spawns harness\nscripts with `bash -lc ...` — the **only** `-lc` site in the coder runner. The `-l` is load-bearing: harness binaries\n(codex/claude/gemini) live on the nvm/npm-global PATH that only the login profile sets. **Never drop `-l` to make a\ntest faster.**\n\nConsequence: any test that spawns a real harness script pays ~10 s before its script runs a single line. Measured\nend-to-end for `$spawnLoggedBashScript.test.ts`: **12.66 s from spawn to first heartbeat**, then only 1.8 s for the\nactual process-tree termination being asserted.\n\n**Why:** this is a machine/environment cost that has nothing to do with the behavior under test, so it must be\nbudgeted separately. Reusing one timeout constant for both \"wait for the fixture to boot\" and \"wait for the asserted\nbehavior\" is what made `$spawnLoggedBashScript.test.ts` flake — a 20 s budget with 12.7 s already spent on shell boot\nblows up as soon as a second Jest worker (`maxWorkers: 2`) competes for the disk.\n\n**How to apply:** when a `scripts/run-codex-prompts` test times out waiting for a spawned script, do NOT assume the\nproduction logic broke — measure the startup leg first. Give setup waits a generous budget (Jest `testTimeout` is\n5 minutes, so there is room) and keep the tight bound only on the assertion. Also make the wait abort early when the\nwrapper shell exits, printing its exit code / signal / captured output — otherwise a wrapper that dies immediately\nlooks identical to a slow machine. What is left is 10 `npm warn deprecated` lines plus 62\n`npm audit` advisories, so the prompt title says \"peer dependency warnings\" but the work is deprecations + audit.\n\n- Removed `crypto` (deprecated placeholder for the Node built-in, never actually used) and `y-websocket-server`\n  (never imported - `other/y-websocket-server/y-websocket.js` runs it through `npx`).\n- Replaced `glob-promise` with `glob@13` behind one new `src/utils/files/findFilesByGlob.ts` used by all 11 call\n  sites. `glob-promise` pinned `glob@8`, which is what dragged in the deprecated `inflight`. Without\n  restoring both, callers that compare or snapshot filenames break.\n- Version bumps for the advisories: `next`, `express`, `socket.io-client`, `mailparser`, `@aws-sdk/client-s3`,\n  `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `nodemailer` (7 -> 9), `dompurify`, `jspdf`, `postcss`, `express-openapi-validator`\n  (for `multer` 2).\n- **Node engines trap:** `@aws-sdk/client-s3` has no advisory-free release that still allows Node 18 - the fixed\n  versions are `>=20`. That is acceptable *only* because `better-sqlite3`, `@supabase/supabase-js`, `playwright`,\n  `cspell` and `@prisma/studio-core` already excluded Node 18 before this change, so the real floor did not move.\n  Check this the fast way: walk `package-lock.json` `packages['node_modules/<name>'].engines.node` for every direct\n  dep and `semver.satisfies('18.18.0', range, {loose: true})`, comparing `git show HEAD:package-lock.json` against\n  the working tree. Do not write \"no Node version changed\" in the changelog without running that.\n- npm `overrides` are **not** a way out: they apply only to this repo's own install, never to someone installing\n  the published `ptbk`, so they cannot clear a user-facing `npm audit`.\n\nRelated: [[ptbk-browser-bundle-jsdom-task]] (same generator, `browser` field), [[promptbook-verification-step-order]],\n[[coder-bash-login-shell-cost]] (the flake that blocked this task's verification twice)","originalFile":"---\nname: ptbk-install-peer-warnings-task\ndescription: \"\\\"[✨👉] When installing ptbk there are lot of peer dependency warnings\\\" — the zod 3 vs zod 4 split, why @promptbook/cli cannot just drop zod, and the fast --package-lock-only way to reproduce npm ERESOLVE\"\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: ae9faf42-babf-481b-a708-5164f847cb92\n  modified: 2026-09-11T16:15:51.414Z\n---\n\nFixed 2026-09-11. `npm i ptbk` printed 13 `ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` events; 10 of them were zod.\n\n**Root cause (two independent parts):**\n1. The tree contained two irreconcilable zod families — `@ai-sdk/openai@1` / `@ai-sdk/google@1` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@0` peer-require `zod@^3.0.0` (every version of those majors does), while `@openai/agents` peer-requires `zod@^4.0.0` and the Agents Server itself imports zod 4. No single hoisted zod satisfies both. Fixed by upgrading to `@ai-sdk/openai@2.0.127` / `@ai-sdk/google@2.0.97` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@1.0.56` (peer `^3.25.76 || ^4.1.8`).\n2. `bundleReferencesDependency` in `scripts/generate-packages/addDependenciesForGeneratedPackages.ts` substring-matched `from 'x'` anywhere in `packages/*/esm/index.es.js`, so the **code templates inside the transpilers** (`AgentOsTranspiler`, `AnthropicClaudeManagedTranspiler` emit `import { z } from 'zod';` for the *transpiled* project) made `@promptbook/core` publish `zod`, `dotenv` and `@anthropic-ai/sdk` as real dependencies. Fixed by requiring `import`/`export` needles to sit on a line that *starts* with the keyword (rollup always emits real imports at column 0); `require(`/`import(` calls still match anywhere.\n\n**Why:** these traps are invisible from the code — the `zod` pin looks deliberate, and the obvious \"just drop zod from `@promptbook/cli`\" is wrong.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- **Do not** try to remove `zod` (or any root dependency) from `@promptbook/cli`: `rollup.config.js` gives the cli `additionalDependencies: [..., ...Object.keys(dependencies)]`, i.e. *all* root deps, because the cli ships `apps/agents-server` and that app imports zod (`managementApiSchemas.ts`, MCP route). The cli must keep it.\n- **Do not** jump to the newest `@ai-sdk/*`: `@ai-sdk/openai@4` / `google@4` / `deepseek@3` (and `@ai-sdk/provider-utils@5`) declare `engines: node >=22`, which would break the repo's `engines: node >=18.18.0`. The `2.x`/`1.x` line accepts zod 4 and still says `node >=18`.\n- Upgrading past `@ai-sdk/*@1` forces a `LanguageModelV1 → V2` migration of `src/llm-providers/vercel/createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider.ts` (used by Google **and** Deepseek): `provider.chat(modelId)` takes no settings, `doGenerate` loses `inputFormat`/`mode`, the result is `content: Array<{type,...}>` instead of `text`, and usage is `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`. `npm run test-types` verifies all of it because the request is typed `Parameters<typeof model.doGenerate>[0]`.\n- **Reproduce/verify npm warnings in ~1 min instead of ~8:** `npm install ptbk@<version> --package-lock-only --no-audit --no-fund` in a scratch dir — registry metadata only, no tarballs, identical ERESOLVE output. To test a *candidate* manifest, write the generated `packages/cli/package.json` `dependencies` into a local `file:` package and resolve that.\n- Compute the exact conflict list from the lockfile: walk `packages[*].peerDependencies`, resolve each peer by climbing `node_modules` segments, `semver.satisfies(..., {loose: true})` — **`loose` matters**, `@tailwindcss/typography` has an invalid range (`>=3.0.0 || insiders || ...`) that is a false positive without it.\n- 3 warnings are unfixable from here: `swagger-ui-react`'s nested `react-copy-to-clipboard` / `react-debounce-input` / `react-inspector` cap React at 18 and are unmaintained. `swagger-ui-react` is really used (`apps/agents-server/src/app/swagger/SwaggerPageClient.tsx`).\n- `@promptbook/cli` also exposed a separate defect worth knowing: `createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider` calls `model.doGenerate(rawRequest)` **twice** per prompt (double cost, half-counted usage) — reported in `agents-messages/2026-09-1100-vercel-adapter-calls-the-model-twice.message.md`, deliberately not fixed.\n\nRelated: [[ptbk-browser-bundle-jsdom-task]] (same generator, `browser` field), [[promptbook-verification-step-order]]\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":5,"oldLines":7,"newStart":5,"newLines":7,"lines":["   node_type: memory","   type: project","   originSessionId: ae9faf42-babf-481b-a708-5164f847cb92","-  modified: 2026-09-11T16:15:51.414Z","+  modified: 2026-09-17T16:02:57.169Z"," ---"," "," Fixed 2026-09-11. `npm i ptbk` printed 13 `ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` events; 10 of them were zod."]},{"oldStart":25,"oldLines":4,"newStart":25,"newLines":27,"lines":[" - 3 warnings are unfixable from here: `swagger-ui-react`'s nested `react-copy-to-clipboard` / `react-debounce-input` / `react-inspector` cap React at 18 and are unmaintained. `swagger-ui-react` is really used (`apps/agents-server/src/app/swagger/SwaggerPageClient.tsx`)."," - `@promptbook/cli` also exposed a separate defect worth knowing: `createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider` calls `model.doGenerate(rawRequest)` **twice** per prompt (double cost, half-counted usage) — reported in `agents-messages/2026-09-1100-vercel-adapter-calls-the-model-twice.message.md`, deliberately not fixed."," ","-Related: [[ptbk-browser-bundle-jsdom-task]] (same generator, `browser` field), [[promptbook-verification-step-order]]","+**Round 2 (2026-09-17), same prompt number `2026-09-0151` but a different symptom:** the pasted console no longer","+shows any ERESOLVE line - round 1 really did fix those. What is left is 10 `npm warn deprecated` lines plus 62","+`npm audit` advisories, so the prompt title says \"peer dependency warnings\" but the work is deprecations + audit.","+","+- Removed `crypto` (deprecated placeholder for the Node built-in, never actually used) and `y-websocket-server`","+  (never imported - `other/y-websocket-server/y-websocket.js` runs it through `npx`).","+- Replaced `glob-promise` with `glob@13` behind one new `src/utils/files/findFilesByGlob.ts` used by all 11 call","+  sites. `glob-promise` pinned `glob@8`, which is what dragged in the deprecated `inflight`. The wrapper exists","+  because glob 9+ dropped two guarantees glob 8 had: **`/` separators on Windows** and **sorted output**. Without","+  restoring both, callers that compare or snapshot filenames break.","+- Version bumps for the advisories: `next`, `express`, `socket.io-client`, `mailparser`, `@aws-sdk/client-s3`,","+  `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `nodemailer` (7 -> 9), `dompurify`, `jspdf`, `postcss`, `express-openapi-validator`","+  (for `multer` 2).","+- **Node engines trap:** `@aws-sdk/client-s3` has no advisory-free release that still allows Node 18 - the fixed","+  versions are `>=20`. That is acceptable *only* because `better-sqlite3`, `@supabase/supabase-js`, `playwright`,","+  `cspell` and `@prisma/studio-core` already excluded Node 18 before this change, so the real floor did not move.","+  Check this the fast way: walk `package-lock.json` `packages['node_modules/<name>'].engines.node` for every direct","+  dep and `semver.satisfies('18.18.0', range, {loose: true})`, comparing `git show HEAD:package-lock.json` against","+  the working tree. Do not write \"no Node version changed\" in the changelog without running that.","+- npm `overrides` are **not** a way out: they apply only to this repo's own install, never to someone installing","+  the published `ptbk`, so they cannot clear a user-facing `npm audit`.","+","+Related: [[ptbk-browser-bundle-jsdom-task]] (same generator, `browser` field), [[promptbook-verification-step-order]],","+[[coder-bash-login-shell-cost]] (the flake that blocked this task's verification twice)"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"memdirStamped":true}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Sjo1en6CAVhsMz5hhQ7Ewq","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\Users\\me\\.claude\\projects\\C--Users-me-work-ai-promptbook\\memory\\ptbk-install-peer-warnings-task.md has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8f44f218-fe4b-4504-acd8-438e13a0f15f","uuid":"86e92c31-940f-407f-a9e5-b613ba27382f","timestamp":"2026-09-17T16:03:03.762Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\.claude\\projects\\C--Users-me-work-ai-promptbook\\memory\\ptbk-install-peer-warnings-task.md","oldString":"description: \"\\\"[✨👉] When installing ptbk there are lot of peer dependency warnings\\\" — the zod 3 vs zod 4 split, why @promptbook/cli cannot just drop zod, and the fast --package-lock-only way to reproduce npm ERESOLVE\"","newString":"description: \"\\\"[✨👉] When installing ptbk there are lot of peer dependency warnings\\\" — round 1 (ERESOLVE: the zod 3 vs zod 4 split, why @promptbook/cli cannot drop zod, --package-lock-only repro) and round 2 (npm warn deprecated + npm audit: glob-promise -> findFilesByGlob, and the @aws-sdk Node-18 engines trap)\"","originalFile":"---\nname: ptbk-install-peer-warnings-task\ndescription: \"\\\"[✨👉] When installing ptbk there are lot of peer dependency warnings\\\" — the zod 3 vs zod 4 split, why @promptbook/cli cannot just drop zod, and the fast --package-lock-only way to reproduce npm ERESOLVE\"\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: ae9faf42-babf-481b-a708-5164f847cb92\n  modified: 2026-09-17T16:02:57.169Z\n---\n\nFixed 2026-09-11. `npm i ptbk` printed 13 `ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` events; 10 of them were zod.\n\n**Root cause (two independent parts):**\n1. The tree contained two irreconcilable zod families — `@ai-sdk/openai@1` / `@ai-sdk/google@1` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@0` peer-require `zod@^3.0.0` (every version of those majors does), while `@openai/agents` peer-requires `zod@^4.0.0` and the Agents Server itself imports zod 4. No single hoisted zod satisfies both. Fixed by upgrading to `@ai-sdk/openai@2.0.127` / `@ai-sdk/google@2.0.97` / `@ai-sdk/deepseek@1.0.56` (peer `^3.25.76 || ^4.1.8`).\n2. `bundleReferencesDependency` in `scripts/generate-packages/addDependenciesForGeneratedPackages.ts` substring-matched `from 'x'` anywhere in `packages/*/esm/index.es.js`, so the **code templates inside the transpilers** (`AgentOsTranspiler`, `AnthropicClaudeManagedTranspiler` emit `import { z } from 'zod';` for the *transpiled* project) made `@promptbook/core` publish `zod`, `dotenv` and `@anthropic-ai/sdk` as real dependencies. Fixed by requiring `import`/`export` needles to sit on a line that *starts* with the keyword (rollup always emits real imports at column 0); `require(`/`import(` calls still match anywhere.\n\n**Why:** these traps are invisible from the code — the `zod` pin looks deliberate, and the obvious \"just drop zod from `@promptbook/cli`\" is wrong.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- **Do not** try to remove `zod` (or any root dependency) from `@promptbook/cli`: `rollup.config.js` gives the cli `additionalDependencies: [..., ...Object.keys(dependencies)]`, i.e. *all* root deps, because the cli ships `apps/agents-server` and that app imports zod (`managementApiSchemas.ts`, MCP route). The cli must keep it.\n- **Do not** jump to the newest `@ai-sdk/*`: `@ai-sdk/openai@4` / `google@4` / `deepseek@3` (and `@ai-sdk/provider-utils@5`) declare `engines: node >=22`, which would break the repo's `engines: node >=18.18.0`. The `2.x`/`1.x` line accepts zod 4 and still says `node >=18`.\n- Upgrading past `@ai-sdk/*@1` forces a `LanguageModelV1 → V2` migration of `src/llm-providers/vercel/createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider.ts` (used by Google **and** Deepseek): `provider.chat(modelId)` takes no settings, `doGenerate` loses `inputFormat`/`mode`, the result is `content: Array<{type,...}>` instead of `text`, and usage is `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`. `npm run test-types` verifies all of it because the request is typed `Parameters<typeof model.doGenerate>[0]`.\n- **Reproduce/verify npm warnings in ~1 min instead of ~8:** `npm install ptbk@<version> --package-lock-only --no-audit --no-fund` in a scratch dir — registry metadata only, no tarballs, identical ERESOLVE output. To test a *candidate* manifest, write the generated `packages/cli/package.json` `dependencies` into a local `file:` package and resolve that.\n- Compute the exact conflict list from the lockfile: walk `packages[*].peerDependencies`, resolve each peer by climbing `node_modules` segments, `semver.satisfies(..., {loose: true})` — **`loose` matters**, `@tailwindcss/typography` has an invalid range (`>=3.0.0 || insiders || ...`) that is a false positive without it.\n- 3 warnings are unfixable from here: `swagger-ui-react`'s nested `react-copy-to-clipboard` / `react-debounce-input` / `react-inspector` cap React at 18 and are unmaintained. `swagger-ui-react` is really used (`apps/agents-server/src/app/swagger/SwaggerPageClient.tsx`).\n- `@promptbook/cli` also exposed a separate defect worth knowing: `createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider` calls `model.doGenerate(rawRequest)` **twice** per prompt (double cost, half-counted usage) — reported in `agents-messages/2026-09-1100-vercel-adapter-calls-the-model-twice.message.md`, deliberately not fixed.\n\n**Round 2 (2026-09-17), same prompt number `2026-09-0151` but a different symptom:** the pasted console no longer\nshows any ERESOLVE line - round 1 really did fix those. What is left is 10 `npm warn deprecated` lines plus 62\n`npm audit` advisories, so the prompt title says \"peer dependency warnings\" but the work is deprecations + audit.\n\n- Removed `crypto` (deprecated placeholder for the Node built-in, never actually used) and `y-websocket-server`\n  (never imported - `other/y-websocket-server/y-websocket.js` runs it through `npx`).\n- Replaced `glob-promise` with `glob@13` behind one new `src/utils/files/findFilesByGlob.ts` used by all 11 call\n  sites. `glob-promise` pinned `glob@8`, which is what dragged in the deprecated `inflight`. The wrapper exists\n  because glob 9+ dropped two guarantees glob 8 had: **`/` separators on Windows** and **sorted output**. Without\n  restoring both, callers that compare or snapshot filenames break.\n- Version bumps for the advisories: `next`, `express`, `socket.io-client`, `mailparser`, `@aws-sdk/client-s3`,\n  `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `nodemailer` (7 -> 9), `dompurify`, `jspdf`, `postcss`, `express-openapi-validator`\n  (for `multer` 2).\n- **Node engines trap:** `@aws-sdk/client-s3` has no advisory-free release that still allows Node 18 - the fixed\n  versions are `>=20`. That is acceptable *only* because `better-sqlite3`, `@supabase/supabase-js`, `playwright`,\n  `cspell` and `@prisma/studio-core` already excluded Node 18 before this change, so the real floor did not move.\n  Check this the fast way: walk `package-lock.json` `packages['node_modules/<name>'].engines.node` for every direct\n  dep and `semver.satisfies('18.18.0', range, {loose: true})`, comparing `git show HEAD:package-lock.json` against\n  the working tree. Do not write \"no Node version changed\" in the changelog without running that.\n- npm `overrides` are **not** a way out: they apply only to this repo's own install, never to someone installing\n  the published `ptbk`, so they cannot clear a user-facing `npm audit`.\n\nRelated: [[ptbk-browser-bundle-jsdom-task]] (same generator, `browser` field), [[promptbook-verification-step-order]],\n[[coder-bash-login-shell-cost]] (the flake that blocked this task's verification twice)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":11,"newStart":1,"newLines":11,"lines":[" ---"," name: ptbk-install-peer-warnings-task","-description: \"\\\"[✨👉] When installing ptbk there are lot of peer dependency warnings\\\" — the zod 3 vs zod 4 split, why @promptbook/cli cannot just drop zod, and the fast --package-lock-only way to reproduce npm ERESOLVE\"","+description: \"\\\"[✨👉] When installing ptbk there are lot of peer dependency warnings\\\" — round 1 (ERESOLVE: the zod 3 vs zod 4 split, why @promptbook/cli cannot drop zod, --package-lock-only repro) and round 2 (npm warn deprecated + npm audit: glob-promise -> findFilesByGlob, and the @aws-sdk Node-18 engines trap)\""," metadata: ","   node_type: memory","   type: project","   originSessionId: ae9faf42-babf-481b-a708-5164f847cb92","-  modified: 2026-09-17T16:02:57.169Z","+  modified: 2026-09-17T16:03:03.736Z"," ---"," "," Fixed 2026-09-11. `npm i ptbk` printed 13 `ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` events; 10 of them were zod."]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"memdirStamped":true}}

zod 3 (`@ai-sdk/*@1`) vs zod 4 (`@openai/agents` + agents-server) is irreconcilable, `@promptbook/cli` cannot drop zod (it gets *all* root deps), newest `@ai-sdk/*` needs Node 22; plus the `--package-lock-only` 1-minute repro recipe","newString":"- [ptbk install peer-warnings task](ptbk-install-peer-warnings-task.md) — \"[✨👉] lot of peer dependency warnings when installing `ptbk`\": round 1 (2026-09-11, ERESOLVE/zod 3-vs-4, `--package-lock-only` repro) and round 2 (2026-09-17, `npm warn deprecated` + `npm audit`: `glob-promise`→`findFilesByGlob`, and the `@aws-sdk` Node-18 engines trap)","originalFile":"# Memory Index\n\n- [Agents Server fix-live task](agents-server-fix-live-task.md) — recurring \"[✨😢] Fix `live.ptbk.io`\" (nginx \"Server is getting ready\" fallback = Next app not listening): root cause found 2026-09-03 was `pm2 jlist` output (6.4 MB) blowing a 1 MB `execFile` maxBuffer, which silently skipped the delete-before-start guard and duplicated project runtimes until the VPS ran out of threads; includes the diagnostic recipe and the on-box recovery steps\n- [Agents Server implicit FROM @Adam task](agents-server-implicit-from-adam-task.md) — recurring \"[✨🟥] Every agent should implicitly inherit from `@Adam`\": the inheritance code was always right; root cause (found 2026-08-21) was `getAgentPermanentId` resolving a name to a **soft-deleted namesake** after a core agent was reinstated — plus how to diagnose \"works locally, broken on live\" via public routes\n- [Agents Server projects default-running task](agents-server-projects-default-running-task.md) — recurring \"default state of the agent project should be running\": IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-19 via `desired-states.json` (absent = running) + boot/5-min autostart pass; nginx resolves project ports per request so apply-domains only runs when a domain actually changes\n- [Agents Server project card task](agents-server-project-card-task.md) — recurring \"project card with nice title and icon\": IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-07 (check working tree first); resolve in createAgentProjectInfo only; favicon route is login-gated and SSR img errors are lost before hydration\n- [Goal-chat planned messages task](agents-server-goal-chat-planned-messages-task.md) — recurring \"agent says he planned a message but there are none\" / \"should work like setInterval\": planning goes via the `messages/planned/<message>.json` sidecar (AgentKit `set_timeout` tools are dead code) and planned messages now repeat by re-arming the same timeout row in place\n- [ptbk coder --git-changes task](ptbk-coder-git-changes-task.md) — \"[✨🛼] Allow to pick what happen with dirty working dir\": IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-29 (`--ignore-git-changes` removed); the three traps = shared `addPromptRunnerExecutionOptions`, the dead `createCoderRunOptionsForAgent` bridge, and the `[^]` line being rewritten every step\n- [ptbk coder prompt-checkbox task](ptbk-coder-prompt-checkbox-task.md) — recurring \"[✨🤺] allow prompts with no `[ ]`\": round 1 (unmarked = todo) + round 2 (`[.]` alias, `ptbk-coder-ignore`); choke points are `parsePromptFile` + `loadPromptFiles`, and the ignore marker is own-line only so the prompt file that documents it does not ignore itself\n- [ptbk coder harness install-method task](ptbk-coder-harness-install-method-task.md) — \"[✨🕗] ptbk coder npm-updates a standalone Codex\": IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-04 (check working tree first); choke points = `HarnessDefinition.standaloneInstallation` + `resolveHarnessInstallationMethodFromPaths` + `resolveHarnessUpdatePlan`; `unknown` never falls back to npm; probe real origins via a throwaway jest test, not ts-node\n- [ptbk coder init no-override task](ptbk-coder-init-no-override-task.md) — \"[✨🤲] coder init overrides scripts in `package.json`/`settings.json`\": IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-11; single choke point is `mergeStringRecordJsonFile` (now additive-only + returns `addedEntryKeys`), plus the referenced-artifact model that creates `developer.book`/`AGENTS.md`/`common.md` only with the script that points at them\n- [ptbk coder qwen-code harness task](ptbk-coder-qwen-code-harness-task.md) — \"[✨🆓] Add `qwen-code` harness\": IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-02; adding any harness is driven by `CLI_AGENT_HARNESS_NAMES` alone, the `qwen` CLI has **no** reasoning-effort flag (so `--thinking-level` is not forwarded, like `gemini`), and `.vscode/terminals.json` is permission-gated so the agent cannot edit it\n- [Promptbook prettier baseline](promptbook-prettier-baseline.md) — repo is NOT clean under its declared prettier 2.8.8; don't chase `prettier --check` failures on files you didn't touch\n- [Verification step order](promptbook-verification-step-order.md) — `test-for-ptbk-coder` = 10 ordered steps, aborts at first failure; a `test-unit` failure leaves agents-server lint + Next build unrun; suite-wall-clock≈whole-run timeout = suspended host, not a regression\n- [Jest EPERM verification flake](promptbook-jest-eperm-verification-flake.md) — `test-for-ptbk-coder` dying at `test-unit` with `kill EPERM` after all tests pass is environmental (Windows teardown), not your diff; fixed via `scripts/ignore-kill-eperm.js` preload\n- [Coder bash login-shell cost](coder-bash-login-shell-cost.md) — `bash -lc` costs ~9.5s here (nvm in `~/.bash_profile`) and `-l` is load-bearing for harness PATH; budget coder-test setup waits separately from the asserted behavior\n- [Agents Server show-progress task](agents-server-show-progress-task.md) — recurring \"show real progress of the agent\" chat prompt: runner is a separate process, the only live signal is its stream-json runtime log on the shared folder; wire via resolveAgentMessageRuntimeActivity → progressCard (never static/fake text)\n- [Agents Server System-menu warnings gating](agents-server-system-warnings-gating.md) — resolveHeaderSystemWarnings choke point gates admin-only ⚠️ (resource/core-agents/Shibboleth);
